# luminous_ui — Project Docs & Continuation System

This `docs/` tree is the **durable memory of the project**. It exists so any new
Claude Code session (or human) can resume work **without reloading the whole
codebase into context**. Read this file first, then load only the docs relevant
to your task.

> **These docs are a guide, not a rulebook.** They capture the current best plan
> and the *reasoning* behind it — not a fixed process to execute blindly. If,
> while working, the code or new context reveals a better or simpler approach,
> **propose it**: say what you'd change and why, and (once it's the direction)
> update the affected doc + record the shift in `decisions.md`. The plans exist
> to be improved, not obeyed. What must be preserved is the *rationale* and the
> *update trail*, so the next session understands why things are the way they are.

## New session? Resume protocol

1. Read **`progress.md`** — the single source of truth for *what's done, what's
   in flight, and where to pick up* (the **Resume point**).
2. Skim **`roadmap.md`** for the big picture (the five phases).
3. Open only the **`workstreams/<area>.md`** you're working on, plus any
   **`reference/`** file it points to. Do **not** read the other workstreams.
4. Follow **`conventions.md`** — especially the sub-agent policy and the
   end-of-session doc-update ritual.

## File map

| File | What it's for |
|---|---|
| `progress.md` | Living status + session log + the current **resume point**. Update every session. |
| `roadmap.md` | The phased plan (P1→P5) and dependencies. |
| `decisions.md` | Decision log (why we chose what) + locked assumptions. |
| `conventions.md` | How we work: sub-agents, doc ritual, code/test/commit rules. |
| `workstreams/backend-data.md` | **P1** — Bun+Hono API, tcgdex→D1 ingest, R2 images, auth, deck API, lobby DO. Contains the tcgdex API reference. |
| `workstreams/deck-builder.md` | **P2** — real cards in the builder, richer filters, editor + decks list. |
| `workstreams/simulator.md` | **P3** — the rules-driven game engine. |
| `workstreams/online.md` | **P4** — run the simulator over the lobby DO for real matches. |
| `workstreams/polish.md` | **P5** — profiles, avatars, lobby names, misc refinement. |
| `reference/ptcg-rules.md` | Condensed Pokémon TCG ruleset — the spec for the simulator (P3). |

## The one rule that keeps this working

**Keep context small.** Delegate research, code-mapping, and multi-file edits to
sub-agents (see `conventions.md`), load only the workstream you need, and write
what you learned back into these docs **before the session ends**.

# Roadmap

Five phases. Each has a detailed workstream doc; this is the map + dependencies.
Live status lives in `progress.md`, not here.

## Phase 1 — Backend & Data Foundation → `workstreams/backend-data.md`
Stand up the Bun + Hono API on Cloudflare. Ingest real tcgdex card data into D1,
mirror images to R2, add accounts + auth (email/password + Discord/Google),
persist decks/folders, and stand up the lobby Durable Object (WebSocket) server.
**Unblocks everything else.**

## Phase 2 — Deck Builder & Decks List (real cards) → `workstreams/deck-builder.md`
Replace the fixture card pool with the live catalog API. Complete the deck
editor (add/remove, counts, format validation, save/load) and the decks list
page (folders, CRUD, persistence). Upgrade filters using the richer tcgdex
fields (set/serie, rarity, HP, illustrator, regulation mark, ability/attack text,
energy cost).
*Depends on: P1 catalog + deck API.*

## Phase 3 — Simulator Engine → `workstreams/simulator.md`
Research the official Pokémon TCG rules (`reference/ptcg-rules.md`) and build the
game engine: a deterministic state machine + a card-effect system driven by the
imported card data + descriptions. Iterative — accuracy improves pass over pass;
unimplemented cards degrade gracefully. The goal is to replicate the real game.
*Depends on: P2 (real, usable decks) + the ruleset.*

## Phase 4 — Online Matches → `workstreams/online.md`
Run the P3 engine authoritatively inside the lobby Durable Object so two players
on different machines can play a real game. Swap the client lobby transport from
BroadcastChannel to WebSocket. Same engine as local play, with tweaks for
authority/hidden info.
*Depends on: P3 engine + P1 lobby DO.*

## Phase 5 — Polish → `workstreams/polish.md`
Now that user + card data exist: player names & profile pictures on the lobby,
profiles, real deck-cover art, and general refinement. Threads through P2–P4 but
tracked separately so it isn't forgotten.
*Depends on: P1 user data.*

1	# Working Conventions
2	
3	## Guidance, not gospel
4	These docs are a **living guide**, not a fixed process. You have context the
5	planning sessions didn't — the actual code, real data, what just broke. Use it:
6	- **Suggest better/different approaches** when you see them. Don't follow a task
7	  list off a cliff because it's written down.
8	- When you deviate: **explain the what + why**, prefer aligning with the user on
9	  anything significant, then **update the affected doc** and log the change in
10	  `decisions.md` (with its rationale). Small in-the-flow improvements don't need
11	  ceremony — just keep the docs honest.
12	- Locked assumptions and D-numbered decisions are **defaults with reasons**, not
13	  laws. Revisit any of them freely; the only hard rule is *don't reverse one
14	  silently* — leave a trail.
15	- Treat file/symbol references in these docs as **point-in-time** — verify against
16	  the current code before relying on them.
17	
18	## Context hygiene (the point of this whole system)
19	- Load **`progress.md` + the one relevant `workstreams/*.md`** (+ its
20	  `reference/`). Don't read unrelated workstreams or sweep the repo.
21	- Prefer facts already written in these docs over re-deriving them.
22	
23	## Sub-agent / workflow policy
24	Delegate to sub-agents to keep the main session's context lean:
25	- **Research** (rules, library docs, API behaviour) → a `general-purpose` agent
26	  that writes a condensed doc into `reference/` and returns only a summary.
27	- **Code mapping** ("how does X work today, what's missing") → an **Explore**
28	  agent (read-only; returns conclusions, not file dumps).
29	- **Implementation** of a self-contained slice → a `general-purpose` agent with
30	  a tight spec; it edits files and returns a summary + what to verify.
31	- **Review** before committing non-trivial work → `/code-review`.
32	- **Big fan-out** (e.g. authoring effect handlers for many cards, or a broad
33	  audit) → a **Workflow** (multi-agent). Note: user-triggered/opt-in — ask first.
34	
35	Rule of thumb: if answering would mean reading many files, delegate it and keep
36	only the conclusion.
37	
38	## Code & quality
39	- TypeScript strict; match the surrounding code's style and comment density.
40	- **Biome** for lint/format; **Vitest** for tests. Run **`bun run check`**
41	  (tsc + biome lint + vitest) before calling work done.
42	- Pure logic gets unit tests (see the many `*.test.ts` in the repo); DOM tests
43	  opt into jsdom per-file (`// @vitest-environment jsdom`).
44	
45	## Git / commits
46	- Branch off `main` for non-trivial work; commit/push only when asked.
47	- Commit trailer per global config: `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...`.
48	
49	## End-of-session ritual (do not skip)
50	1. Update `progress.md`: status table + session-log entry + **new resume point**.
51	2. Record any decision in `decisions.md`.
52	3. Write anything learned into the right workstream/reference doc so the next
53	   session doesn't rediscover it.
54

# Working Conventions

## Guidance, not gospel
These docs are a **living guide**, not a fixed process. You have context the
planning sessions didn't — the actual code, real data, what just broke. Use it:
- **Suggest better/different approaches** when you see them. Don't follow a task
  list off a cliff because it's written down.
- When you deviate: **explain the what + why**, prefer aligning with the user on
  anything significant, then **update the affected doc** and log the change in
  `decisions.md` (with its rationale). Small in-the-flow improvements don't need
  ceremony — just keep the docs honest.
- Locked assumptions and D-numbered decisions are **defaults with reasons**, not
  laws. Revisit any of them freely; the only hard rule is *don't reverse one
  silently* — leave a trail.
- Treat file/symbol references in these docs as **point-in-time** — verify against
  the current code before relying on them.

## Context hygiene (the point of this whole system)
- Load **`progress.md` + the one relevant `workstreams/*.md`** (+ its
  `reference/`). Don't read unrelated workstreams or sweep the repo.
- Prefer facts already written in these docs over re-deriving them.

## Sub-agent / workflow policy
Delegate to sub-agents to keep the main session's context lean:
- **Research** (rules, library docs, API behaviour) → a `general-purpose` agent
  that writes a condensed doc into `reference/` and returns only a summary.
- **Code mapping** ("how does X work today, what's missing") → an **Explore**
  agent (read-only; returns conclusions, not file dumps).
- **Implementation** of a self-contained slice → a `general-purpose` agent with
  a tight spec; it edits files and returns a summary + what to verify.
- **Review** before committing non-trivial work → `/code-review`.
- **Big fan-out** (e.g. authoring effect handlers for many cards, or a broad
  audit) → a **Workflow** (multi-agent). Note: user-triggered/opt-in — ask first.

Rule of thumb: if answering would mean reading many files, delegate it and keep
only the conclusion.

## Code & quality
- TypeScript strict; match the surrounding code's style and comment density.
- **Biome** for lint/format; **Vitest** for tests. Run **`bun run check`**
  (tsc + biome lint + vitest) before calling work done.
- Pure logic gets unit tests (see the many `*.test.ts` in the repo); DOM tests
  opt into jsdom per-file (`// @vitest-environment jsdom`).

## Git / commits
- Branch off `main` for non-trivial work; commit/push only when asked.
- Commit trailer per global config: `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...`.

## End-of-session ritual (do not skip)
1. Update `progress.md`: status table + session-log entry + **new resume point**.
2. Record any decision in `decisions.md`.
3. Write anything learned into the right workstream/reference doc so the next

They were mock chrome from the /simulator prototype, so 13 "history navigation is unreachable during your own turn:action" described 14 navigation that did not exist. Two buttons a screen reader announced as 15 "Previous"/"Forward" and that did nothing are worse than none; they are gone. 16 If a real history is built, they come back WIRED. 17 - **The playmat's ⟶ was enabled exactly when the panel covered it** — the panel 18 renders precisely when `passDisabled === false` — so on /play and online it 19 was never clickable. `PlaymatView.onPassTurn` is now OPTIONAL and the control 20 renders only for a driver that passes one: the /simulator sandbox, where 21 nothing covers it. Each game panel has carried its own `Pass` since the 22 earlier fix, browser-verified. 23 Verified in a browser at 1280×700 with a real `elementFromPoint` hit-test (a 24 synthetic `.click()` is what hid the original bug): at a live turn:action /play 25 has no "Pass turn" and no arrows, its in-panel `Pass` hit-tests to itself and 26 advances the turn; /simulator still has its ⟶, hit-testing to itself. 27 - **Lobby identity — NAMES DONE 2026-07-26 (P5-1, D81); avatars still open.** A 28 lobby seat's name is now the ACCOUNT's `displayName`, resolved SERVER-SIDE at 29 the hello (`loadDisplayName`, apps/api/src/lobby/displayName.ts) from the same 30 `userId` the /ws session cookie already provided — so it is authoritative, not 31 announced, and a player cannot present themselves as someone else. An anonymous 32 socket (or an account whose name is blank) keeps the client's generated 33 "Player 4271" handle; the blank case deliberately does NOT fall back to the 34 email, which `AccountButton` shows a user about themselves but which a lobby 35 broadcasts to the opponent AND to spectators. The client announces its account 36 name too, purely so the host's locally-seeded waiting screen doesn't flash the 37 old handle. Browser-verified: signed-in seats read "Ash"/"Misty" across panels, 38 turn banner, game log and the spectator pill, while two signed-out players kept 39 their generated handles. **AVATARS (generated) DONE 2026-07-26 (P5-2, D82):** 40 `PlayerState.avatarSeed` carries an FNV-1a HASH of the account id (never the id 41 — the snapshot is broadcast to the opponent and to spectators), from which 42 `PlayerAvatar` draws a deterministic two-hue gradient plus the same initial the 43 account control shows. Nothing stored, nothing uploaded, and the same person 44 looks the same to you in every lobby; an anonymous seat keeps the generic 45 figure rather than being given a face that would change next visit. Saturation 46 and lightness are FIXED so the seed picks the hue and never how loud the result 47 is. **Still open: uploaded avatars** — the item below (R2 + CSP); an image 48 simply wins over the generated one when it lands. 49 - **Profiles — NAME + FACE DONE 2026-07-26 (P5-5, D85); favourite deck open.** 50 The Profile section on **/settings** (`src/features/settings/ 51 ProfileSection.tsx`) is where an account edits itself, and the first thing it 52 fixes is that P5-1 made your name authoritative and broadcast while leaving it 53 unchangeable. **`PATCH /auth/me`** (requireUser BEFORE the validator; no write 54 when nothing changed) takes `updateProfileRequestSchema` — one required 55 `displayName`, trimmed, 1–64, the same bounds register applies to its optional 56 one. The provider's `updateProfile` adopts the api's answer as the current 57 user, so the corner account control follows with no re-probe. 58 **The section shows the REAL generated avatar, not a lookalike:** `userSchema` 59 now carries **`avatarSeed`** (derived server-side, the same value the lobby 60 broadcasts), so `PlayerAvatar` — moved to `src/components/` since two surfaces 61 use it — draws the identical face here and in a lobby. The seed module moved 62 with it, to `apps/api/src/auth/avatar.ts`: it is a property of the ACCOUNT, not 63 of a seat. Deriving the hash client-side was rejected — a second copy of FNV-1a 64 is one that must agree with the server forever. 65 The initial follows the draft as you type; a 401 mid-save re-probes and the 66 panel becomes a sign-in prompt (`state.from` returns you here). **A rename 67 reaches a lobby at the next hello** (`loadDisplayName` resolves the seat name 68 there), so a player already seated keeps the old name until they rejoin. 69 Browser-verified across two clients: "Brock" → "Pewter Brock" updated the 70 initial, the corner control and the OPPONENT's player panel, with a 71 byte-identical gradient throughout (the seed is the id, not the name). 72 **FAVOURITE DECK — DONE 2026-07-27 (P5-7, D87):** an account pins one of its 73 **own** decks as its favourite (nullable `users.favourite_deck_id`, migration 74 `0005`, surfaced as `userSchema.favouriteDeckId` — just the ID) and sees that 75 deck's cover + name on /settings via a native `

I have the picture. The resume point offers a P5 backlog choice:
1. **Uploaded avatars** — biggest, but explicitly needs a *product decision* (moderation) from the user → not an autonomous pick.
2. **Card detail view** — richer tcgdex fields; self-contained, no product call needed.

I'm working in the luminous_ui repo (a Pokémon TCG web app: Bun+Hono API on Cloudflare with D1, and a Vite/React web app). I need you to map the current code so I can decide the minimal coherent slice. Do NOT edit anything — read-only.

Report back CONCISELY (conclusions, not file dumps) on:

1. **Card data model — what's actually available.** Find the D1 schema for cards (likely apps/api/src/**/schema*.ts or a drizzle schema) and the catalog/cards API endpoints. Which tcgdex fields are ingested and queryable per card? Specifically: does the DB store attacks, abilities, weaknesses/resistances, retreat cost, pricing, illustrator, set/serie, regulation mark, rarity, HP, types, evolvesFrom, national dex number, flavor/description text? List what's present vs absent. Point me at the exact schema file + the API route file(s) that serve card data (e.g. GET /cards, GET /cards/:id).

2. **Is there a single-card GET endpoint?** Or only list/search? What shape does a card come back as (the zod/TS type name and file)?

3. **Current card display on the web.** Where are cards rendered today (the deck builder card grid, search results)? Find the card component(s) (e.g. a CardTile/CardImage). Is there ANY existing detail/modal/popover view for a card, or only the image tile? Where would a detail view naturally slot in (what triggers it — click on a card in the builder?).

4. **Shared types.** Is there a shared package (e.g. packages/schema or apps/shared) where card types + zod schemas live and are imported by both API and web? Name it and the card type export.

5. **A recommended minimal slice.** Given all the above, what's the smallest coherent "card detail view" that leaves the repo better — e.g. a modal opened from the deck builder showing the big image + attacks/abilities/set/illustrator? Flag anything MISSING that would block it (e.g. attacks not ingested into D1, or no single-card endpoint) since that would balloon the scope.

6. **Secondary, brief:** grep for `prefers-reduced-motion` usage across the web app (src/**). Roughly how many surfaces respect it, and do the newest P5 surfaces (src/features/settings/**, the deck cover picker/CoverDialog, PlayerAvatar) reference it? Just a rough count + which files — this is a fallback slice I'm weighing.

Be thorough on #1–#3 (that's the crux), concise elsewhere.

1	// Catalog tables — ingested from tcgdex (§3.4), read-only to the app.
2	// Spec: docs/workstreams/backend-data.md §5.3. Source shapes: the Zod models
3	// in @luminous/schema (packages/schema/src/tcgdex/*), authored against live
4	// payloads — every column here maps 1:1 onto a field of those schemas.
5	//
6	// Conventions:
7	// - ids are tcgdex ids, stored as text PKs ("sv" / "sv01" / "sv01-001").
8	// - `*_url` asset columns store the tcgdex ORIGIN base URLs, extensionless
9	//   (§4.4) — NOT R2 URLs. Images are mirrored into R2 lazily by the
10	//   `/assets/*` Worker routes (cache-aside), which use these bases on a miss.
11	// - Catalog dates/timestamps stay ISO TEXT, verbatim from tcgdex ("YYYY-MM-DD"
12	//   dates; `cards.updated` mixes `Z` and `+HH:MM` offsets). User-data tables
13	//   use integer epoch ms instead — see ./users.ts.
14	// - Structured sub-shapes persist as JSON text (`mode: "json"`), typed with
15	//   the tcgdex types so ingest round-trips without hand mapping.
16	//
17	// Deliberately NOT stored (revisit when a feature needs them):
18	// - `variants_detailed` — per-physical-print foil/stamp/per-print pricing;
19	//   irrelevant to the app today (we keep the 5-flag `variants_json`).
20	// - `pricing` — volatile market aggregates, not catalog data.
21	// - `boosters` — documented upstream, never observed on live `en` payloads.
22	// - dp/neo-era Pokémon extras (`level`, `item`, `suffix`, `description`,
23	//   `dexId`) — no app feature reads them; the schema stays full-history
24	//   *capable* (nothing breaks when old sets are ingested, these fields are
25	//   simply not persisted).
26	
27	import type { TcgdexAbility, TcgdexAttack, TcgdexVariants, TcgdexWeakRes } from "@luminous/schema";
28	import { index, integer, sqliteTable, text } from "drizzle-orm/sqlite-core";
29	
30	export const series = sqliteTable("series", {
31	  id: text("id").primaryKey(),
32	  name: text("name").notNull(),
33	  /** "YYYY-MM-DD"; optional upstream (used to order series chronologically). */
34	  releaseDate: text("release_date"),
35	  /** tcgdex origin logo base URL, extensionless (§4.4: append `.png`/`.webp`). */
36	  logoUrl: text("logo_url"),
37	});
38	
39	export const sets = sqliteTable(
40	  "sets",
41	  {
42	    id: text("id").primaryKey(),
43	    serieId: text("serie_id")
44	      .notNull()
45	      .references(() => series.id),
46	    name: text("name").notNull(),
47	    /** tcgdex origin logo/symbol base URLs, extensionless (§4.4: append `.png`/`.webp`). */
48	    logoUrl: text("logo_url"),
49	    symbolUrl: text("symbol_url"),
50	    /** "YYYY-MM-DD", required upstream. */
51	    releaseDate: text("release_date").notNull(),
52	    countTotal: integer("count_total").notNull(),
53	    countOfficial: integer("count_official").notNull(),
54	    legalStandard: integer("legal_standard", { mode: "boolean" }).notNull(),
55	    legalExpanded: integer("legal_expanded", { mode: "boolean" }).notNull(),
56	    /** PTCGO set code (e.g. swsh3 → "DAA"); only PTCGO-era sets have one. */
57	    tcgOnline: text("tcg_online"),
58	  },
59	  (t) => [index("sets_serie_id_idx").on(t.serieId)],
60	);
61	
62	export const cards = sqliteTable(
63	  "cards",
64	  {
65	    id: text("id").primaryKey(),
66	    setId: text("set_id")
67	      .notNull()
68	      .references(() => sets.id),
69	    localId: text("local_id").notNull(),
70	    name: text("name").notNull(),
71	    category: text("category", { enum: ["Pokemon", "Trainer", "Energy"] }).notNull(),
72	    illustrator: text("illustrator"),
73	    rarity: text("rarity"),
74	    regulationMark: text("regulation_mark"),
75	
76	    // Pokémon-only fields (null on Trainer/Energy).
77	    hp: integer("hp"),
78	    stage: text("stage"),
79	    evolveFrom: text("evolve_from"),
80	    /** Energy types, e.g. ["Grass"]. */
81	    typesJson: text("types_json", { mode: "json" }).$type<string[]>(),
82	    retreat: integer("retreat"),
83	    abilitiesJson: text("abilities_json", { mode: "json" }).$type<TcgdexAbility[]>(),
84	    attacksJson: text("attacks_json", { mode: "json" }).$type<TcgdexAttack[]>(),
85	    weaknessesJson: text("weaknesses_json", { mode: "json" }).$type<TcgdexWeakRes[]>(),
86	    resistancesJson: text("resistances_json", { mode: "json" }).$type<TcgdexWeakRes[]>(),
87	
88	    // Trainer/Energy-only fields.
89	    trainerType: text("trainer_type"),
90	    energyType: text("energy_type"),
91	    /** Trainer/Energy rules text (absent on basic energies). */
92	    effect: text("effect"),
93	
94	    // `legal` is optional upstream; ingest maps a missing block to false/false.
95	    legalStandard: integer("legal_standard", { mode: "boolean" }).notNull(),
96	    legalExpanded: integer("legal_expanded", { mode: "boolean" }).notNull(),
97	    /** The 5 print-run flags {normal, reverse, holo, firstEdition, wPromo}. */
98	    variantsJson: text("variants_json", { mode: "json" }).$type<TcgdexVariants>(),
99	    /** tcgdex origin image base URL, extensionless (§4.4: append `/high.webp` etc.). */
100	    imageUrl: text("image_url"),
101	    /** tcgdex `updated` ISO timestamp, verbatim — ingest skips unchanged rows. */
102	    updated: text("updated"),
103	  },
104	  (t) => [index("cards_set_id_idx").on(t.setId), index("cards_name_idx").on(t.name)],
105	);

1	// D1 row → canonical catalog domain mapping (P1 milestone 5, §5.2/§6).
2	//
3	// The inverse altitude of ../ingest/map.ts (tcgdex payload → row): here rows
4	// come back out as the domain shapes in @luminous/schema/catalog. Pure —
5	// routes.ts owns the queries — so every branch unit-tests as a plain function.
6	//
7	// Asset rewriting is the one real transform: rows store tcgdex ORIGIN base
8	// URLs (extensionless, §4.4), the domain stores OUR asset base paths
9	// (`/assets/cards/{id}`, `/assets/sets/{id}`) served by the lazy R2 mirror.
10	// A path is emitted ONLY when the corresponding origin column is non-null —
11	// a card with image_url NULL maps to `image: null`, and a set missing just
12	// its logo gets `logo: null` while keeping `symbol`.
13	
14	// The domain `Set` is aliased locally so it can't be confused with the global.
15	import type {
16	  Card,
17	  CardBrief,
18	  Serie,
19	  SerieBrief,
20	  Set as CatalogSet,
21	  SetBrief,
22	} from "@luminous/schema";
23	import { cards, type series, type sets } from "../db/schema";
24	
25	export type CardRow = typeof cards.$inferSelect;
26	export type SetRow = typeof sets.$inferSelect;
27	export type SerieRow = typeof series.$inferSelect;
28	
29	/** The card columns a CardBrief needs — pass to `db.select(...)` so list
30	    queries never drag the BIG JSON blobs (attacks/abilities/…) off disk.
31	    `types_json` rides along: it's a few quoted words, and the builder's
32	    tiles and kind filters need it (M9). The two legality flags joined for
33	    P2 — the deck validator reads `legal` off hydrated lists. */
34	export const cardBriefColumns = {
35	  id: cards.id,
36	  name: cards.name,
37	  category: cards.category,
38	  rarity: cards.rarity,
39	  imageUrl: cards.imageUrl,
40	  setId: cards.setId,
41	  localId: cards.localId,
42	  typesJson: cards.typesJson,
43	  hp: cards.hp,
44	  regulationMark: cards.regulationMark,
45	  stage: cards.stage,
46	  trainerType: cards.trainerType,
47	  energyType: cards.energyType,
48	  legalStandard: cards.legalStandard,
49	  legalExpanded: cards.legalExpanded,
50	};
51	export type CardBriefRow = Pick<CardRow, keyof typeof cardBriefColumns>;
52	
53	/** OUR card-image base path (clients append `/{quality}.{ext}`, §4.4). */
54	function cardImagePath(cardId: string): string {
55	  return `/assets/cards/${cardId}`;
56	}
57	
58	/** OUR set-asset base path (clients append `/logo.{ext}` / `/symbol.{ext}`). */
59	function setAssetPath(setId: string): string {
60	  return `/assets/sets/${setId}`;
61	}

65	    id: row.id,
66	    name: row.name,

68	    rarity: row.rarity,

70	    setId: row.setId,
71	    localId: row.localId,

1	// The canonical domain Card (D5 — docs/workstreams/backend-data.md §5.2).
2	//
3	// MODELING CHOICE — one flat object, not the tcgdex discriminated union: the
4	// D1 rows (§5.3) already flatten the three categories into one table where
5	// every category-specific column is NULL off-category, and the read API
6	// serves that reality verbatim. Consumers still narrow on `category`; a flat
7	// shape just spares them a union round-trip for fields that are `null`
8	// either way. Nullability mirrors the DB exactly: TEXT/INTEGER nullable
9	// columns → `.nullable()`, NOT NULL columns → required.
10	//
11	// ASSET CONVENTION — `image` is OUR asset base path, `/assets/cards/{id}`
12	// (or null when the card has no scan). Clients append `/{quality}.{ext}`
13	// with quality ∈ high|low and ext ∈ webp|png|jpg — the same suffix rule as
14	// tcgdex origin URLs (§4.4) — and the Worker's GET /assets/cards/:id/:file
15	// route mirrors + serves the bytes. tcgdex origin URLs never leave the API.
16	
17	import { z } from "zod";
18	import { legalSchema } from "./common";
19	
20	export const cardCategorySchema = z.enum(["Pokemon", "Trainer", "Energy"]);
21	export type CardCategory = z.infer<typeof cardCategorySchema>;
22	
23	/** The nine types Basic Energy cards have been printed for, in the canonical
24	    wheel order — the one basic-energy vocabulary of the monorepo (the engine
25	    derives energy provision from it, the deck builder its type palette).
26	    Fairy is retired (Sword & Shield era) but its prints remain in the pool.
27	    Dragon and Colorless are deliberately NOT here: both appear as cost/type
28	    entries, but Dragon has no Basic Energy and Colorless is a cost symbol,
29	    not an attachable basic type. */
30	export const BASIC_ENERGY_TYPES = [
31	  "Grass",
32	  "Fire",
33	  "Water",
34	  "Lightning",
35	  "Psychic",
36	  "Fighting",
37	  "Darkness",
38	  "Metal",
39	  "Fairy",
40	] as const;
41	export type BasicEnergyType = (typeof BASIC_ENERGY_TYPES)[number];
42	
43	// The nested blocks persist as JSON columns typed with the tcgdex shapes, so
44	// these domain twins are structurally identical to their Tcgdex* namesakes —
45	// stored JSON round-trips through them unchanged.
46	
47	/** An attack. `damage` is a number OR a modifier string ("60+", "20×"). */
48	export const attackSchema = z.object({
49	  cost: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
50	  name: z.string(),
51	  effect: z.string().optional(),
52	  damage: z.union([z.number(), z.string()]).optional(),
53	});
54	export type Attack = z.infer<typeof attackSchema>;
55	
56	/** An ability block (`type` is "Ability", or era labels like "Poke-POWER"). */
57	export const abilitySchema = z.object({
58	  type: z.string().optional(),
59	  name: z.string(),
60	  effect: z.string().optional(),
61	});
62	export type Ability = z.infer<typeof abilitySchema>;
63	
64	/** A weakness or resistance. `value` is a modifier string: "×2", "+20", "-30". */
65	export const weakResSchema = z.object({
66	  type: z.string(),
67	  value: z.string().optional(),
68	});
69	export type WeakRes = z.infer<typeof weakResSchema>;
70	
71	/** Which print runs a card exists in. */
72	export const variantsSchema = z.object({
73	  normal: z.boolean().optional(),
74	  reverse: z.boolean().optional(),
75	  holo: z.boolean().optional(),
76	  firstEdition: z.boolean().optional(),
77	  wPromo: z.boolean().optional(),
78	});
79	export type Variants = z.infer<typeof variantsSchema>;
80	
81	/** List/search projection of a card — what GET /cards and `set.cards` serve.
82	    Beyond identity + art it carries exactly the flat card-table columns the
83	    deck builder's tiles and client-side "kind" filters read (M9), plus the
84	    `legal` block the deck validator needs on hydrated lists (P2): energy
85	    types, hp, regulation mark and the per-category subtype discriminators.
86	    No JSON blobs (attacks/abilities/…) and no set join — those stay on the
87	    full Card / future projections. */

89	  id: z.string(),
90	  name: z.string(),
91	  category: cardCategorySchema,
92	  rarity: z.string().nullable(),
93	  /** OUR asset base path `/assets/cards/{id}` (append `/{quality}.{ext}`), or null. */
94	  image: z.string().nullable(),
95	  setId: z.string(),
96	  localId: z.string(),

13	| D7 | Game engine placement | Separate **`packages/engine`** (pure logic) — imported by both `apps/web` (local play) and `apps/api` (authoritative DO). *Why: the engine runs in two runtimes; an app can't import another app.* |
14	| D8 | Card-effect modeling | **Composable, data-driven op programs** over shared archetype templates (not per-card functions); engine emits **semantic events** consumed by the animation layer. *Why: cards are minor variations on a few archetypes; keeps authoring + animation cheap. Detail in `workstreams/simulator.md`.* |
15	| D9 | Image mirroring & ingest execution (refines D4/§3.4) | Images mirror into R2 **lazily** — a Worker route (`GET /assets/…`) serves from R2 and on miss fetches tcgdex origin, stores, streams; catalog rows keep tcgdex **origin** URLs. Card-data backfill runs as a **local Bun script** applying batched upsert SQL via `wrangler d1 execute`; a future cron does small in-Worker deltas only. *Why: a full SV backfill is ~10k images — over Worker subrequest limits in one shot and hours of CLI puts; cache-aside mirrors exactly what's viewed and stays within limits.* (2026-07-09) |

# Decisions & Locked Assumptions

## Product / architecture decisions
| # | Decision | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Backend data strategy | Own DB — ingest tcgdex → Cloudflare D1, serve our own API |
| D2 | Accounts & persistence | Full accounts + auth; users own their decks |
| D2a | Auth methods | Email + password **and** social OAuth (Discord + Google) |
| D3 | Catalog scope | Full-history-capable schema, ingest SV-era first |
| D4 | Card images | Mirror into R2, serve from our domain |
| D5 | Card type | Unify — one canonical `Card`; builder/playmat are view projections |
| D6 | Online lobby server | In scope — real Durable Object (WebSocket) lobby |
| D7 | Game engine placement | Separate **`packages/engine`** (pure logic) — imported by both `apps/web` (local play) and `apps/api` (authoritative DO). *Why: the engine runs in two runtimes; an app can't import another app.* |
| D8 | Card-effect modeling | **Composable, data-driven op programs** over shared archetype templates (not per-card functions); engine emits **semantic events** consumed by the animation layer. *Why: cards are minor variations on a few archetypes; keeps authoring + animation cheap. Detail in `workstreams/simulator.md`.* |
| D9 | Image mirroring & ingest execution (refines D4/§3.4) | Images mirror into R2 **lazily** — a Worker route (`GET /assets/…`) serves from R2 and on miss fetches tcgdex origin, stores, streams; catalog rows keep tcgdex **origin** URLs. Card-data backfill runs as a **local Bun script** applying batched upsert SQL via `wrangler d1 execute`; a future cron does small in-Worker deltas only. *Why: a full SV backfill is ~10k images — over Worker subrequest limits in one shot and hours of CLI puts; cache-aside mirrors exactly what's viewed and stays within limits.* (2026-07-09) |

## Card detail view — codebase map

### 1. Card data model — what D1 actually stores

**Schema file:** `/home/jofre/projects/luminous_ui/apps/api/src/db/schema.ts` (the `cards` table, lines 62–105). Re-exported via `apps/api/src/db/catalog.ts`.

Per-card columns actually ingested and queryable:

| Field | Stored? | Column |
|---|---|---|
| name, category (Pokemon/Trainer/Energy) | Yes | `name`, `category` |
| HP | Yes | `hp` (null off-Pokémon) |
| types | Yes | `typesJson` (JSON string[]) |
| attacks | Yes | `attacksJson` (JSON `TcgdexAttack[]`: cost, name, effect, damage) |
| abilities | Yes | `abilitiesJson` (JSON `TcgdexAbility[]`: type, name, effect) |
| weaknesses / resistances | Yes | `weaknessesJson`, `resistancesJson` (type + value modifier) |
| retreat cost | Yes | `retreat` (integer) |
| illustrator | Yes | `illustrator` |
| rarity | Yes | `rarity` |
| regulation mark | Yes | `regulationMark` |
| stage | Yes | `stage` |
| evolvesFrom | Yes | `evolveFrom` |
| trainer/energy rules text | Yes | `effect` (Trainer/Energy only; null on Pokémon and basic energies) |
| trainerType / energyType | Yes | `trainerType`, `energyType` |
| variants (5 print-run flags) | Yes | `variantsJson` |
| legality (standard/expanded) | Yes | `legalStandard`, `legalExpanded` |
| image base | Yes | `imageUrl` (tcgdex origin base; served via `/assets/cards/{id}`) |
| set / serie | **Partial** | only `setId` FK. Set name/logo live in `sets`, serie in `series` — the card row/Card shape does NOT join them (see note below). |

**Deliberately ABSENT** (documented in the schema header comment, lines 17–25 — "revisit when a feature needs them"):
- **pricing** — not stored ("volatile market aggregates, not catalog data").
- **national dex number** (`dexId`) — not stored.
- **flavor/description text** (`description`) — not stored.
- `variants_detailed`, `boosters`, and dp/neo extras (`level`, `item`, `suffix`).

So of your wishlist, **pricing, national dex number, and flavor text are the only three blockers** — everything else (attacks, abilities, weak/resist, retreat, illustrator, HP, types, evolvesFrom, regulation mark, rarity) is already in D1.

Mapping/serving code: `apps/api/src/catalog/map.ts` (`mapCardRow`, lines 82–108 → full `Card`; `mapCardBriefRow` → `CardBrief`), routes in `apps/api/src/catalog/routes.ts`, query builder in `apps/api/src/catalog/query.ts`. Ingest mapping in `apps/api/src/ingest/map.ts`.

### 2. Single-card GET endpoint — yes, it already exists

`GET /cards/:id` — `apps/api/src/catalog/routes.ts` lines 137–147. KV-cached, returns the full **`Card`** shape (404 on unknown id). `GET /cards` is the paginated list returning `CardBrief[]` (no JSON blobs — briefs deliberately omit attacks/abilities to keep list queries light).

- **Full card type:** `Card` / `cardSchema` in `/home/jofre/projects/luminous_ui/packages/schema/src/catalog/card.ts` (lines 112–146). Nested block schemas `attackSchema`, `abilitySchema`, `weakResSchema`, `variantsSchema` live in the same file. `Card` carries attacks/abilities/weaknesses/resistances/retreat/illustrator/effect/variants — everything from #1.
- **Brief type:** `CardBrief` / `cardBriefSchema` (lines 88–109) — identity + art + tile fields only.
- **Web client already wraps it:** `getCard(id): Promise<Card>` in `/home/jofre/projects/luminous_ui/src/lib/api.ts` (lines 215–218), and it's **already consumed** by `src/features/game/cardPool.ts`. So the endpoint is live and battle-tested on the web side.

### 3. Current card display on the web

**The only catalog-card component is the tile.** Cards render in the deck builder's center grid:
- `/home/jofre/projects/luminous_ui/src/features/builder/components/CardGrid.tsx` — `CardGrid` + inner `CardTile` (lines 50–134). Each tile is a `<button>` wrapping `CardImage` (low-quality scan). **Click = add a copy to the deck; right-click = remove.** Tilt/juice via `useTiltJuice`. There is a `pulse` shake but **no detail/modal/popover** — clicking never opens any richer view.
- Card image primitive: `/home/jofre/projects/luminous_ui/src/components/CardImage.tsx` (fill + fixed modes, graceful fallback).
- The builder's card view-model is `BuilderCard` (`src/features/builder/cards.ts`, lines 45–69) — adapted from `CardBrief` in `src/features/builder/catalog.ts`. It has NO attacks/abilities (briefs don't carry them).

**Where a detail view slots in:** the natural trigger is the `CardTile` in `CardGrid.tsx`. The catch: click and right-click are already taken by add/remove. You'd need a distinct affordance — e.g. a long-press, an info-button overlay on hover, or (cleanest) reserve click for "open detail" and move add to a `+` button. That interaction decision is the main design question, not a data one.

**No existing tcgdex-attack rendering anywhere.** The `attacks`/`abilities`/`retreat` seen in `GameHud.tsx`/`OnlineHud.tsx` come from the game **engine's `program`**, not the catalog Card's tcgdex fields — so a detail view would be the first surface to render tcgdex attack/ability text. No component to reuse there.

### 4. Shared types

Package **`@luminous/schema`** (`/home/jofre/projects/luminous_ui/packages/schema`), imported by both API and web. Card types: **`Card` / `cardSchema`** and **`CardBrief` / `cardBriefSchema`** in `packages/schema/src/catalog/card.ts`. The API boundary-parses with the zod schemas; the web client is types-only (imports `Card` as a type, trusts the wire). The `*Json` DB columns are typed with the raw `Tcgdex*` twins in `packages/schema/src/tcgdex/*`.

### 5. Recommended minimal slice

**A card-detail modal opened from the builder grid, hydrating via the existing `getCard(id)`.** Nothing is blocked on the backend for the good version:

- Reuse the established native-`<dialog>` modal pattern — copy `CoverDialog.tsx` / `ImportExportDialog.tsx` (`showModal()`/`close()` driven by an `open` prop; free focus-trap, Escape, backdrop-dismiss). Glass styling helpers already exist: `GLASS_DIALOG_PANEL`, `GLASS_DIALOG_GHOST_BUTTON` in `src/lib/glass.ts`. Use `ScrollArea` for overflow.
- Content from the full `Card`: big high-quality image (`cardImageUrl(id, "high")`), name/HP/types (reuse `EnergyGlyph` in `src/features/builder/components/EnergyGlyph.tsx` for type + attack-cost pips), attacks (cost pips + damage + effect), abilities, weakness/resistance/retreat, illustrator, rarity, regulation mark, and Trainer/Energy `effect` text.
- Wiring: add an `onInspect(card)` affordance to `CardTile` (see the interaction caveat in #3), lift `open`/`selectedId` state into `CardGrid` or `DeckBuilder.tsx`, fetch on open with `getCard`. The `getCard` client fn and its test already exist, so this is purely a web-UI addition.

**Scope flags:**
- **Do NOT promise pricing, national dex number, or flavor text** — none are in D1. Adding any one balloons scope into a schema migration + a re-ingest of ~3.7k rows + updating `cardSchema`, `mapCardRow`, and `ingest/map.ts`. Keep the slice to fields already stored.
- **Set/serie names are one extra hop.** The `Card` payload gives only `setId`/`localId`, not the set's display name/logo or the serie. Showing "Scarlet & Violet · Paldea Evolved 081/193" needs a second `getSet(setId)` (or `getSeries()`) call, or you settle for `setId`/`localId` text. Minor, but don't assume the set name is in the card response.

### 6. Secondary — `prefers-reduced-motion` coverage

**~12 files reference it** across the web app (grep of `src/**` for `prefers-reduced-motion` / `useReducedMotion` / `reducedMotion`):

`src/index.css`, `src/components/useTiltJuice.ts`, `src/features/background/glowRenderer.ts`, `src/features/decks/useFlip.ts`, `src/features/home/CardSheen.ts`, `src/features/online/online.css`, `src/features/playmat/components/AnimatedCardsLayer.tsx`, `src/features/playmat/pixi/CardView.ts` (heaviest, 22 hits), `src/features/playmat/playmat.css`, `src/lib/animation/ghostDrag.ts`, `src/lib/animation/useGhostDrag.ts`, plus one test. So the motion-heavy surfaces (playmat, home sheen, background glow, tilt, drag, flip) all respect it.

**The newest P5 surfaces do NOT reference it:**
- `src/features/settings/**` (`Settings.tsx`, `ProfileSection.tsx`, `FontProvider.tsx`) — none.
- `src/features/builder/components/CoverDialog.tsx` — none (uses `transition-all hover:scale-[1.03] active:scale-95` unconditionally, line 37).
- `src/components/PlayerAvatar.tsx` — none.

So there's a real, self-contained fallback slice here: these P5 surfaces animate (scale/transition) without honoring the user's reduced-motion preference, unlike the older animation code which consistently does.

Comprehensive map. Decision made: **build the card detail view.** The backend is fully ready (`GET /cards/:id` + `getCard()` already exist and return the full `Card` with attacks/abilities/weak-resist/retreat/illustrator/rarity/regulation mark), it's a genuine P5 feature, and it needs no product call — unlike uploaded avatars (moderation call) and the P4 deploy (credentials). It's meatier than the reduced-motion audit but well-scoped for one session, and I'll respect reduced-motion in the new surface anyway.

1	// The canonical domain Card (D5 — docs/workstreams/backend-data.md §5.2).
2	//
3	// MODELING CHOICE — one flat object, not the tcgdex discriminated union: the
4	// D1 rows (§5.3) already flatten the three categories into one table where
5	// every category-specific column is NULL off-category, and the read API
6	// serves that reality verbatim. Consumers still narrow on `category`; a flat
7	// shape just spares them a union round-trip for fields that are `null`
8	// either way. Nullability mirrors the DB exactly: TEXT/INTEGER nullable
9	// columns → `.nullable()`, NOT NULL columns → required.
10	//
11	// ASSET CONVENTION — `image` is OUR asset base path, `/assets/cards/{id}`
12	// (or null when the card has no scan). Clients append `/{quality}.{ext}`
13	// with quality ∈ high|low and ext ∈ webp|png|jpg — the same suffix rule as
14	// tcgdex origin URLs (§4.4) — and the Worker's GET /assets/cards/:id/:file
15	// route mirrors + serves the bytes. tcgdex origin URLs never leave the API.
16	
17	import { z } from "zod";
18	import { legalSchema } from "./common";
19	
20	export const cardCategorySchema = z.enum(["Pokemon", "Trainer", "Energy"]);
21	export type CardCategory = z.infer<typeof cardCategorySchema>;
22	
23	/** The nine types Basic Energy cards have been printed for, in the canonical
24	    wheel order — the one basic-energy vocabulary of the monorepo (the engine
25	    derives energy provision from it, the deck builder its type palette).
26	    Fairy is retired (Sword & Shield era) but its prints remain in the pool.
27	    Dragon and Colorless are deliberately NOT here: both appear as cost/type
28	    entries, but Dragon has no Basic Energy and Colorless is a cost symbol,
29	    not an attachable basic type. */
30	export const BASIC_ENERGY_TYPES = [
31	  "Grass",
32	  "Fire",
33	  "Water",
34	  "Lightning",
35	  "Psychic",
36	  "Fighting",
37	  "Darkness",
38	  "Metal",
39	  "Fairy",
40	] as const;
41	export type BasicEnergyType = (typeof BASIC_ENERGY_TYPES)[number];
42	
43	// The nested blocks persist as JSON columns typed with the tcgdex shapes, so
44	// these domain twins are structurally identical to their Tcgdex* namesakes —
45	// stored JSON round-trips through them unchanged.
46	
47	/** An attack. `damage` is a number OR a modifier string ("60+", "20×"). */
48	export const attackSchema = z.object({
49	  cost: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
50	  name: z.string(),
51	  effect: z.string().optional(),
52	  damage: z.union([z.number(), z.string()]).optional(),
53	});
54	export type Attack = z.infer<typeof attackSchema>;
55	
56	/** An ability block (`type` is "Ability", or era labels like "Poke-POWER"). */
57	export const abilitySchema = z.object({
58	  type: z.string().optional(),
59	  name: z.string(),
60	  effect: z.string().optional(),
61	});
62	export type Ability = z.infer<typeof abilitySchema>;
63	
64	/** A weakness or resistance. `value` is a modifier string: "×2", "+20", "-30". */
65	export const weakResSchema = z.object({
66	  type: z.string(),
67	  value: z.string().optional(),
68	});
69	export type WeakRes = z.infer<typeof weakResSchema>;
70	
71	/** Which print runs a card exists in. */
72	export const variantsSchema = z.object({
73	  normal: z.boolean().optional(),
74	  reverse: z.boolean().optional(),
75	  holo: z.boolean().optional(),
76	  firstEdition: z.boolean().optional(),
77	  wPromo: z.boolean().optional(),
78	});
79	export type Variants = z.infer<typeof variantsSchema>;
80	
81	/** List/search projection of a card — what GET /cards and `set.cards` serve.
82	    Beyond identity + art it carries exactly the flat card-table columns the
83	    deck builder's tiles and client-side "kind" filters read (M9), plus the
84	    `legal` block the deck validator needs on hydrated lists (P2): energy
85	    types, hp, regulation mark and the per-category subtype discriminators.
86	    No JSON blobs (attacks/abilities/…) and no set join — those stay on the
87	    full Card / future projections. */
88	export const cardBriefSchema = z.object({
89	  id: z.string(),
90	  name: z.string(),
91	  category: cardCategorySchema,
92	  rarity: z.string().nullable(),
93	  /** OUR asset base path `/assets/cards/{id}` (append `/{quality}.{ext}`), or null. */
94	  image: z.string().nullable(),
95	  setId: z.string(),
96	  localId: z.string(),
97	  /** Energy types, e.g. ["Grass"] (Pokémon only). */
98	  types: z.array(z.string()).nullable(),
99	  hp: z.number().int().nullable(),
100	  regulationMark: z.string().nullable(),
101	  /** Pokémon stage, tcgdex vocabulary ("Basic" | "Stage1" | "Stage2" | …). */
102	  stage: z.string().nullable(),
103	  /** Trainer subtype ("Item" | "Supporter" | "Stadium" | "Tool" | …). */
104	  trainerType: z.string().nullable(),
105	  /** Energy subtype ("Normal" | "Special"). */
106	  energyType: z.string().nullable(),
107	  legal: legalSchema,
108	});
109	export type CardBrief = z.infer<typeof cardBriefSchema>;
110	
111	/** The one canonical Card (D5) — everything the catalog persists for a card. */
112	export const cardSchema = z.object({
113	  /** tcgdex id, e.g. "sv06.5-001" — our canonical card id. */
114	  id: z.string(),
115	  setId: z.string(),
116	  localId: z.string(),
117	  name: z.string(),
118	  category: cardCategorySchema,
119	  /** OUR asset base path `/assets/cards/{id}` (append `/{quality}.{ext}`), or null. */
120	  image: z.string().nullable(),
121	  illustrator: z.string().nullable(),
122	  rarity: z.string().nullable(),
123	  regulationMark: z.string().nullable(),
124	
125	  // Pokémon-only (null on Trainer/Energy).
126	  hp: z.number().int().nullable(),
127	  stage: z.string().nullable(),
128	  evolveFrom: z.string().nullable(),
129	  /** Energy types, e.g. ["Grass"]. */
130	  types: z.array(z.string()).nullable(),
131	  retreat: z.number().int().nullable(),
132	  abilities: z.array(abilitySchema).nullable(),

input.prompt:
You are implementing a **card detail view** in the luminous_ui repo (a Pokémon TCG web app; Vite/React + TS strict + Tailwind + Biome + Vitest). It's a self-contained web-UI slice. The backend is already fully ready — do NOT touch the API, DB, schema, or ingest. Work only in `src/`.

## What to build
A **card-detail modal**, opened from a card in the deck builder's center grid, that shows a rich single-card view (big image + attacks/abilities/weakness/resistance/retreat/illustrator/rarity/regulation mark/effect text). Data comes from the already-existing `getCard(id)` client fn.

## Ground truth you MUST read first (don't guess)
- `src/features/builder/components/CardGrid.tsx` — the grid + `CardTile`. The tile is a `<button>` (click = add a copy, right-click = remove, onPointerDown = drag start). You will ADD an inspect affordance here.
- `src/features/builder/components/CoverDialog.tsx` — **COPY THIS PATTERN EXACTLY** for the native `<dialog>` (showModal/close driven by an `open` prop; onClose; backdrop click-to-dismiss; close button; glass styling).
- `src/features/builder/components/EnergyGlyph.tsx` — `<EnergyGlyph type={...} className="h-4 w-4" />`. `type` is the `EnergyType` union imported from `src/features/builder/cards.ts` — READ that file to get the exact union and the `BuilderCard` shape (fields: `cardId`, `name`, `hasImage`, …). The glyph keys are: Grass, Fire, Water, Lightning, Psychic, Fighting, Darkness, Metal, Dragon, Colorless.
- `packages/schema/src/catalog/card.ts` — the `Card` type shape (already read for you; summary below). `card.types`, `attack.cost` are `string[]` of type-name strings that MAY include values outside the `EnergyType` union — you must guard (render a text chip fallback for unknown values).
- `src/lib/api.ts` — `getCard(id: string): Promise<Card>` (line ~215) and `cardImageUrl(id, quality)` (quality is "high" | "low"). Use `getCard` to hydrate and `cardImageUrl(id, "high")` for the big image.
- `src/lib/glass.ts` — reuse `GLASS_DIALOG_PANEL`, `GLASS_DIALOG_GHOST_BUTTON`, `FOCUS_RING_INSET`, `GLASS_GHOST_BUTTON`.
- `src/components/ScrollArea.tsx` — for the scrollable details column (see its use in CoverDialog).
- `src/components/CardImage.tsx` — the image primitive (fill mode; graceful fallback). Use it for the big image.
- `src/components/icons.tsx` (or wherever `XIcon`, `CheckIcon` come from in CoverDialog) — find an appropriate "info"/"magnifier"/"search" icon for the inspect button; if none fits, add a small new icon following the existing icon style in that file, or reuse an existing one (e.g. a magnifier/info glyph). Prefer reusing.
- Find where `CardGrid` is rendered (grep for `<CardGrid` / `CardGridProps` — likely `src/features/builder/DeckBuilder.tsx`). That parent will own the modal state.

The `Card` shape (from `packages/schema/src/catalog/card.ts`): `{ id, setId, localId, name, category: "Pokemon"|"Trainer"|"Energy", image, illustrator, rarity, regulationMark, hp, stage, evolveFrom, types (string[]|null), retreat (int|null), abilities ({type?,name,effect?}[]|null), attacks ({cost?:string[],name,effect?,damage?:number|string}[]|null), weaknesses/resistances ({type,value?}[]|null), trainerType, energyType, effect (Trainer/Energy rules text|null), legal, variants }`.

## Component: `src/features/builder/components/CardDetailDialog.tsx`
Props (mirror CoverDialog's mount-always-toggle-via-open style):
```ts
export interface CardDetailDialogProps {
  open: boolean;
  /** The card to show — retained during the close so content doesn't blank out. Null before first open. */
  card: BuilderCard | null;
  onClose: () => void;
}
```
Behavior:
- Native `<dialog>` exactly like CoverDialog (useRef + useEffect on `open` → showModal()/close(); onClose; backdrop click-to-dismiss; aria-labelledby a useId title; close button in the header).
- When `open` and `card` is set, fetch the full card with `getCard(card.cardId)` in an effect keyed on `card.cardId` (only fetch while open). Track `{ status: "loading"|"ready"|"error", data?: Card }`. **Guard against a stale response**: if the effect re-runs or unmounts, ignore the resolved promise (a cancelled flag). Show the known `card.name` in the header immediately (seed), so the header never flashes empty.
- **Loading**: header name (from the seed) + a subtle "Loading…" / skeleton in the body. **Error**: "Couldn't load card details" + a Retry button that re-runs the fetch.
- **Ready** — render:
  - Two-column on ≥sm (`sm:grid-cols-[...]`), stacked on mobile. Left: big image via `<CardImage fill imageUrl={card.hasImage ? cardImageUrl(id,"high") : undefined} .../>` in an `aspect-[2.5/3.5]` box. Right: a `ScrollArea` with the details.
  - Header block: name (big), a category chip, HP (Pokémon), and small chips for rarity + regulation mark when present.
  - Type pips: for each of `types`, render `<EnergyGlyph>` IF the string is a valid glyph key, else a small text chip. Write a tiny type-guard `isGlyphType(s: string): s is EnergyType` (a Set of the 10 keys) — put it in the dialog file or a small helper module; it must be unit-testable, so if it's a pure helper consider a named export.
  - Attacks (Pokémon): each attack as a row — a line of cost pips (map `attack.cost` strings through the same glyph/guard), the attack `name`, the `damage` right-aligned (render number or the modifier string as-is), and `effect` text beneath in muted color. Handle empty/no attacks gracefully (omit the section).
  - Abilities: each — a label from `ability.type` (fallback "Ability"), the `name`, and `effect`.
  - Weakness / Resistance / Retreat: a compact stat row. Weakness/resistance: type glyph (guarded) + `value`. Retreat: the integer (or that many Colorless pips — your call, keep it simple).
  - Trainer/Energy: when `category !== "Pokemon"` and `effect` is set, render the `effect` rules text as a paragraph block.
  - Footer meta: "Illus. {illustrator}" when present, and the set/number as plain text `{localId} · {setId}` (NO set-name lookup — the card payload doesn't carry it; keep it minimal and honest). evolveFrom ("Evolves from {evolveFrom}") when present.
- **Reduced motion**: any transition/scale you add must be gated with Tailwind's `motion-reduce:transition-none` (and avoid scale transforms under reduced motion). This new surface must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- TS strict, match the surrounding comment density and the explanatory-comment style of CoverDialog (a short "why" header comment at the top explaining the two-question interaction and the guard).

## Wiring
1. `CardGridProps`: add `onInspect: (card: BuilderCard) => void;` (required — the grid always offers inspect). Thread it through the `...handlers` spread (note `TileHandlers` is a `Pick<...>` — add `"onInspect"` there so it flows to `CardTile`).
2. `CardTile`: add an **inspect button as a SIBLING of the tile `<button>`**, NOT a child (nesting `<button>` in `<button>` is invalid HTML). Place it as the last child of the `<li className="relative ...">`, absolutely positioned in a corner (e.g. `absolute right-1.5 top-1.5 z-20`), a small round glass button with the info/magnifier icon, `aria-label={`View ${card.name} details`}`. It should be visually subtle and **reveal on hover of the tile AND on its own keyboard focus** — e.g. `opacity-0 focus-visible:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 ...` with `group` added to the `<li>` (or the wrapper), plus `motion-reduce:transition-none`. On click → `onInspect(card)`. It must be keyboard-reachable (it's a real `<button>`, so it is). Ensure `type="button"`. Make sure it sits above the tile button so clicks land on it (z-index), and that clicking it does NOT add a copy (separate element, so it won't — but verify it isn't inside the tile button).
   - Keep the existing add/remove/drag behavior on the tile button 100% intact.
3. Parent (DeckBuilder or wherever CardGrid renders): add state `const [inspecting, setInspecting] = useState<BuilderCard | null>(null)` and `const [detailOpen, setDetailOpen] = useState(false)`. Pass `onInspect={(c) => { setInspecting(c); setDetailOpen(true); }}` to `<CardGrid>`. Render `<CardDetailDialog open={detailOpen} card={inspecting} onClose={() => setDetailOpen(false)} />` alongside the existing dialogs (e.g. next to where CoverDialog / ImportExportDialog are rendered). Keep `inspecting` set through the close so content doesn't blank (mirror how CoverDialog is wired if it uses the same idiom).

## Tests (Vitest)
- Add `src/features/builder/components/CardDetailDialog.test.tsx` with `// @vitest-environment jsdom` at the top. FIRST check whether an existing dialog test (e.g. a CoverDialog/ImportExportDialog `.test.tsx`, grep `showModal` in tests) already establishes how these native-`<dialog>` components are tested under jsdom — MIRROR that setup (jsdom may need `HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal`/`close` spied/mocked). If no dialog test exists, mock `showModal`/`close` on the prototype in a `beforeEach`.
  - Mock `getCard` (from `../../../lib/api`) with `vi.mock`. Test: (a) opening with a card triggers `getCard(cardId)` and renders the name + an attack name + an ability + illustrator once resolved; (b) the loading state shows the seeded name; (c) the error state renders on a rejected `getCard` and Retry re-invokes it; (d) the close button calls `onClose`.
- If you extracted `isGlyphType` as a pure export, add a tiny unit test for it (valid key → true, unknown string like "Colorless"/"Water" true, "Bogus" false) — or fold that assertion into the component test if inline.
- Do NOT weaken or delete existing tests. Match existing test style (look at a neighboring `*.test.tsx`).

## Definitely do NOT
- Do NOT change the API/DB/schema/ingest, or promise pricing / national-dex-number / flavor-text (they are NOT stored — don't reference them).
- Do NOT change the tile's click=add / right-click=remove / drag semantics.
- Do NOT add new npm deps.

## Finish
Run `bunx tsc --noEmit` (or the repo's typecheck) and `bunx biome check` on the files you touched, and run the new test file with `bunx vitest run src/features/builder/components/CardDetailDialog.test.tsx` — get them green. Then return a CONCISE summary: files created/modified, the exact interaction you implemented, any deviation from this spec (with why), and a short "what to verify in the browser" list. Return raw facts, not prose.

Props (mirror CoverDialog's mount-always-toggle-via-open style):
```ts
export interface CardDetailDialogProps {
  open: boolean;
  /** The card to show — retained during the close so content doesn't blank out. Null before first open. */
  card: BuilderCard | null;
  onClose: () => void;
}
```
Behavior:
- Native `<dialog>` exactly like CoverDialog (useRef + useEffect on `open` → showModal()/close(); onClose; backdrop click-to-dismiss; aria-labelledby a useId title; close button in the header).
- When `open` and `card` is set, fetch the full card with `getCard(card.cardId)` in an effect keyed on `card.cardId` (only fetch while open). Track `{ status: "loading"|"ready"|"error", data?: Card }`. **Guard against a stale response**: if the effect re-runs or unmounts, ignore the resolved promise (a cancelled flag). Show the known `card.name` in the header immediately (seed), so the header never flashes empty.
- **Loading**: header name (from the seed) + a subtle "Loading…" / skeleton in the body. **Error**: "Couldn't load card details" + a Retry button that re-runs the fetch.
- **Ready** — render:
  - Two-column on ≥sm (`sm:grid-cols-[...]`), stacked on mobile. Left: big image via `<CardImage fill imageUrl={card.hasImage ? cardImageUrl(id,"high") : undefined} .../>` in an `aspect-[2.5/3.5]` box. Right: a `ScrollArea` with the details.
  - Header block: name (big), a category chip, HP (Pokémon), and small chips for rarity + regulation mark when present.
  - Type pips: for each of `types`, render `<EnergyGlyph>` IF the string is a valid glyph key, else a small text chip. Write a tiny type-guard `isGlyphType(s: string): s is EnergyType` (a Set of the 10 keys) — put it in the dialog file or a small helper module; it must be unit-testable, so if it's a pure helper consider a named export.
  - Attacks (Pokémon): each attack as a row — a line of cost pips (map `attack.cost` strings through the same glyph/guard), the attack `name`, the `damage` right-aligned (render number or the modifier string as-is), and `effect` text beneath in muted color. Handle empty/no attacks gracefully (omit the section).
  - Abilities: each — a label from `ability.type` (fallback "Ability"), the `name`, and `effect`.
  - Weakness / Resistance / Retreat: a compact stat row. Weakness/resistance: type glyph (guarded) + `value`. Retreat: the integer (or that many Colorless pips — your call, keep it simple).
  - Trainer/Energy: when `category !== "Pokemon"` and `effect` is set, render the `effect` rules text as a paragraph block.
  - Footer meta: "Illus. {illustrator}" when present, and the set/number as plain text `{localId} · {setId}` (NO set-name lookup — the card payload doesn't carry it; keep it minimal and honest). evolveFrom ("Evolves from {evolveFrom}") when present.
- **Reduced motion**: any transition/scale you add must be gated with Tailwind's `motion-reduce:transition-none` (and avoid scale transforms under reduced motion). This new surface must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- TS strict, match the surrounding comment density and the explanatory-comment style of CoverDialog (a short "why" header comment at the top explaining the two-question interaction and the guard).

## Wiring
1. `CardGridProps`: add `onInspect: (card: BuilderCard) => void;` (required — the grid always offers inspect). Thread it through the `...handlers` spread (note `TileHandlers` is a `Pick<...>` — add `"onInspect"` there so it flows to `CardTile`).
2. `CardTile`: add an **inspect button as a SIBLING of the tile `<button>`**, NOT a child (nesting `<button>` in `<button>` is invalid HTML). Place it as the last child of the `<li className="relative ...">`, absolutely positioned in a corner (e.g. `absolute right-1.5 top-1.5 z-20`), a small round glass button with the info/magnifier icon, `aria-label={`View ${card.name} details`}`. It should be visually subtle and **reveal on hover of the tile AND on its own keyboard focus** — e.g. `opacity-0 focus-visible:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 ...` with `group` added to the `<li>` (or the wrapper), plus `motion-reduce:transition-none`. On click → `onInspect(card)`. It must be keyboard-reachable (it's a real `<button>`, so it is). Ensure `type="button"`. Make sure it sits above the tile button so clicks land on it (z-index), and that clicking it does NOT add a copy (separate element, so it won't — but verify it isn't inside the tile button).
   - Keep the existing add/remove/drag behavior on the tile button 100% intact.
3. Parent (DeckBuilder or wherever CardGrid renders): add state `const [inspecting, setInspecting] = useState<BuilderCard | null>(null)` and `const [detailOpen, setDetailOpen] = useState(false)`. Pass `onInspect={(c) => { setInspecting(c); setDetailOpen(true); }}` to `<CardGrid>`. Render `<CardDetailDialog open={detailOpen} card={inspecting} onClose={() => setDetailOpen(false)} />` alongside the existing dialogs (e.g. next to where CoverDialog / ImportExportDialog are rendered). Keep `inspecting` set through the close so content doesn't blank (mirror how CoverDialog is wired if it uses the same idiom).

## Tests (Vitest)
- Add `src/features/builder/components/CardDetailDialog.test.tsx` with `// @vitest-environment jsdom` at the top. FIRST check whether an existing dialog test (e.g. a CoverDialog/ImportExportDialog `.test.tsx`, grep `showModal` in tests) already establishes how these native-`<dialog>` components are tested under jsdom — MIRROR that setup (jsdom may need `HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal`/`close` spied/mocked). If no dialog test exists, mock `showModal`/`close` on the prototype in a `beforeEach`.
  - Mock `getCard` (from `../../../lib/api`) with `vi.mock`. Test: (a) opening with a card triggers `getCard(cardId)` and renders the name + an attack name + an ability + illustrator once resolved; (b) the loading state shows the seeded name; (c) the error state renders on a rejected `getCard` and Retry re-invokes it; (d) the close button calls `onClose`.
- If you extracted `isGlyphType` as a pure export, add a tiny unit test for it (valid key → true, unknown string like "Colorless"/"Water" true, "Bogus" false) — or fold that assertion into the component test if inline.
- Do NOT weaken or delete existing tests. Match existing test style (look at a neighboring `*.test.tsx`).

## Definitely do NOT
- Do NOT change the API/DB/schema/ingest, or promise pricing / national-dex-number / flavor-text (they are NOT stored — don't reference them).
- Do NOT change the tile's click=add / right-click=remove / drag semantics.
- Do NOT add new npm deps.

## Finish
Run `bunx tsc --noEmit` (or the repo's typecheck) and `bunx biome check` on the files you touched, and run the new test file with `bunx vitest run src/features/builder/components/CardDetailDialog.test.tsx` — get them green. Then return a CONCISE summary: files created/modified, the exact interaction you implemented, any deviation from this spec (with why), and a short "what to verify in the browser" list. Return raw facts, not prose.

1	// Card model + metadata for the deck builder. The card *data* comes from the
2	// live catalog api (fetched by useCardSearch, adapted in catalog.ts); this
3	// module holds the types, the energy-type palette, the format definitions,
4	// and small pure helpers shared across the builder. Kept pixi-free and
5	// side-effect-free so the pure logic (deckMath, decklistText) and their
6	// tests can import it freely.
7	
8	import { BASIC_ENERGY_TYPES, type BasicEnergyType } from "@luminous/schema";
9	import { ENERGY_COLORS } from "../../lib/energyPalette";
10	
11	/** The energy types the builder filters and paints, in the canonical wheel
12	    order. Derived from the shared basic-energy vocabulary (@luminous/schema)
13	    minus the retired Fairy — old Fairy prints keep adapting to typeless
14	    tiles rather than growing a palette entry — plus Dragon (a Pokémon type
15	    with no Basic Energy) and Colorless (a cost symbol), which exist only in
16	    this UI palette. */
17	export type EnergyType = Exclude<BasicEnergyType, "Fairy"> | "Dragon" | "Colorless";
18	
19	export const ENERGY_TYPES: readonly EnergyType[] = [
20	  ...BASIC_ENERGY_TYPES.filter(
21	    (type): type is Exclude<BasicEnergyType, "Fairy"> => type !== "Fairy",
22	  ),
23	  "Dragon",
24	  "Colorless",
25	];
26	
27	/** Top-level card category — drives the deck-list grouping (Pokémon / Trainer /
28	    Energy) and the right-panel split. Uses the accented "Pokémon" spelling the
29	    game itself uses. */
30	export type Supertype = "Pokémon" | "Trainer" | "Energy";
31	
32	export const SUPERTYPES: Supertype[] = ["Pokémon", "Trainer", "Energy"];
33	
34	// NOTE (P2 task 10): the printed-subtype and rarity vocabularies used to be
35	// hardcoded tuples here (POKEMON_STAGES, TRAINER_SUBTYPES, RARITIES, …). They
36	// now come from the live catalog — GET /facets via useCatalogOptions — so a
37	// card's `subtype` and `rarity` stay plain strings and the rail's chips
38	// reflect what is actually ingested.
39	
40	/** A single browsable card — the builder's view of a catalog card (adapted
41	    from the api shapes in catalog.ts). `cardId` is the tcgdex id ("sv06.5-001"),
42	    also the key of the api's art mirror. Optional fields are absent for
43	    categories they don't apply to (a Trainer has no `types`/`hp`, an Energy
44	    no `hp`, etc.). */
45	export interface BuilderCard {
46	  cardId: string;
47	  name: string;
48	  supertype: Supertype;
49	  /** Basic | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Item | Supporter | Stadium | Pokémon Tool |
50	      Basic Energy | Special Energy — or a newer printed subtype the catalog
51	      knows and this build's tuples don't. */
52	  subtype: string;
53	  /** Energy type(s) — Pokémon (its type) and most Energy cards. */
54	  types?: EnergyType[];
55	  hp?: number;
56	  /** Regulation mark (e.g. "H", "I"), the basis of Standard-format legality. */
57	  regulationMark?: string;
58	  /** Exact catalog rarity string, e.g. "Double rare". */
59	  rarity?: string;
60	  /** Collector number within its set (the catalog's localId, e.g. "081"). */
61	  number?: string;
62	  /** Whether the catalog has a scan for this card — when false, tiles render
63	      the neutral fallback instead of requesting art that would 404. */
64	  hasImage?: boolean;
65	  /** The catalog's structured format-legality verdict (P2) — present on every
66	      api-adapted card; optional only for hand-built fixtures. Groundwork for
67	      validateDeck to stop inferring legality from regulation marks. */
68	  legal?: { standard: boolean; expanded: boolean };
69	}

1	// The canonical domain Card (D5 — docs/workstreams/backend-data.md §5.2).
2	//
3	// MODELING CHOICE — one flat object, not the tcgdex discriminated union: the
4	// D1 rows (§5.3) already flatten the three categories into one table where
5	// every category-specific column is NULL off-category, and the read API
6	// serves that reality verbatim. Consumers still narrow on `category`; a flat
7	// shape just spares them a union round-trip for fields that are `null`
8	// either way. Nullability mirrors the DB exactly: TEXT/INTEGER nullable
9	// columns → `.nullable()`, NOT NULL columns → required.
10	//
11	// ASSET CONVENTION — `image` is OUR asset base path, `/assets/cards/{id}`
12	// (or null when the card has no scan). Clients append `/{quality}.{ext}`
13	// with quality ∈ high|low and ext ∈ webp|png|jpg — the same suffix rule as
14	// tcgdex origin URLs (§4.4) — and the Worker's GET /assets/cards/:id/:file
15	// route mirrors + serves the bytes. tcgdex origin URLs never leave the API.
16	
17	import { z } from "zod";
18	import { legalSchema } from "./common";
19	
20	export const cardCategorySchema = z.enum(["Pokemon", "Trainer", "Energy"]);
21	export type CardCategory = z.infer<typeof cardCategorySchema>;
22	
23	/** The nine types Basic Energy cards have been printed for, in the canonical
24	    wheel order — the one basic-energy vocabulary of the monorepo (the engine
25	    derives energy provision from it, the deck builder its type palette).
26	    Fairy is retired (Sword & Shield era) but its prints remain in the pool.
27	    Dragon and Colorless are deliberately NOT here: both appear as cost/type
28	    entries, but Dragon has no Basic Energy and Colorless is a cost symbol,
29	    not an attachable basic type. */
30	export const BASIC_ENERGY_TYPES = [
31	  "Grass",
32	  "Fire",
33	  "Water",
34	  "Lightning",
35	  "Psychic",
36	  "Fighting",
37	  "Darkness",
38	  "Metal",
39	  "Fairy",
40	] as const;
41	export type BasicEnergyType = (typeof BASIC_ENERGY_TYPES)[number];
42	
43	// The nested blocks persist as JSON columns typed with the tcgdex shapes, so
44	// these domain twins are structurally identical to their Tcgdex* namesakes —
45	// stored JSON round-trips through them unchanged.
46	
47	/** An attack. `damage` is a number OR a modifier string ("60+", "20×"). */
48	export const attackSchema = z.object({
49	  cost: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
50	  name: z.string(),
51	  effect: z.string().optional(),
52	  damage: z.union([z.number(), z.string()]).optional(),
53	});
54	export type Attack = z.infer<typeof attackSchema>;
55	
56	/** An ability block (`type` is "Ability", or era labels like "Poke-POWER"). */
57	export const abilitySchema = z.object({
58	  type: z.string().optional(),
59	  name: z.string(),
60	  effect: z.string().optional(),
61	});
62	export type Ability = z.infer<typeof abilitySchema>;
63	
64	/** A weakness or resistance. `value` is a modifier string: "×2", "+20", "-30". */
65	export const weakResSchema = z.object({
66	  type: z.string(),
67	  value: z.string().optional(),
68	});
69	export type WeakRes = z.infer<typeof weakResSchema>;
70	
71	/** Which print runs a card exists in. */
72	export const variantsSchema = z.object({
73	  normal: z.boolean().optional(),
74	  reverse: z.boolean().optional(),
75	  holo: z.boolean().optional(),
76	  firstEdition: z.boolean().optional(),
77	  wPromo: z.boolean().optional(),
78	});
79	export type Variants = z.infer<typeof variantsSchema>;
80	
81	/** List/search projection of a card — what GET /cards and `set.cards` serve.
82	    Beyond identity + art it carries exactly the flat card-table columns the
83	    deck builder's tiles and client-side "kind" filters read (M9), plus the
84	    `legal` block the deck validator needs on hydrated lists (P2): energy
85	    types, hp, regulation mark and the per-category subtype discriminators.
86	    No JSON blobs (attacks/abilities/…) and no set join — those stay on the
87	    full Card / future projections. */
88	export const cardBriefSchema = z.object({
89	  id: z.string(),
90	  name: z.string(),
91	  category: cardCategorySchema,
92	  rarity: z.string().nullable(),
93	  /** OUR asset base path `/assets/cards/{id}` (append `/{quality}.{ext}`), or null. */
94	  image: z.string().nullable(),
95	  setId: z.string(),
96	  localId: z.string(),
97	  /** Energy types, e.g. ["Grass"] (Pokémon only). */
98	  types: z.array(z.string()).nullable(),
99	  hp: z.number().int().nullable(),
100	  regulationMark: z.string().nullable(),
101	  /** Pokémon stage, tcgdex vocabulary ("Basic" | "Stage1" | "Stage2" | …). */
102	  stage: z.string().nullable(),
103	  /** Trainer subtype ("Item" | "Supporter" | "Stadium" | "Tool" | …). */
104	  trainerType: z.string().nullable(),
105	  /** Energy subtype ("Normal" | "Special"). */
106	  energyType: z.string().nullable(),
107	  legal: legalSchema,
108	});
109	export type CardBrief = z.infer<typeof cardBriefSchema>;
110	
111	/** The one canonical Card (D5) — everything the catalog persists for a card. */
112	export const cardSchema = z.object({
113	  /** tcgdex id, e.g. "sv06.5-001" — our canonical card id. */
114	  id: z.string(),
115	  setId: z.string(),
116	  localId: z.string(),
117	  name: z.string(),
118	  category: cardCategorySchema,
119	  /** OUR asset base path `/assets/cards/{id}` (append `/{quality}.{ext}`), or null. */
120	  image: z.string().nullable(),
121	  illustrator: z.string().nullable(),
122	  rarity: z.string().nullable(),
123	  regulationMark: z.string().nullable(),
124	
125	  // Pokémon-only (null on Trainer/Energy).
126	  hp: z.number().int().nullable(),
127	  stage: z.string().nullable(),
128	  evolveFrom: z.string().nullable(),
129	  /** Energy types, e.g. ["Grass"]. */
130	  types: z.array(z.string()).nullable(),
131	  retreat: z.number().int().nullable(),
132	  abilities: z.array(abilitySchema).nullable(),
133	  attacks: z.array(attackSchema).nullable(),
134	  weaknesses: z.array(weakResSchema).nullable(),
135	  resistances: z.array(weakResSchema).nullable(),
136	
137	  // Trainer/Energy-only.
138	  trainerType: z.string().nullable(),
139	  energyType: z.string().nullable(),
140	  /** Trainer/Energy rules text (null on basic energies and all Pokémon). */
141	  effect: z.string().nullable(),
142	
143	  legal: legalSchema,
144	  variants: variantsSchema.nullable(),
145	});
146	export type Card = z.infer<typeof cardSchema>;

185	  const flank = slot * 0.18; // angular width of each sloped tooth side
186	  const tip = slot * 0.2; // angular width of the (narrow) flat tip

188	    const a = ((deg - 90) * Math.PI) / 180;
189	    return `${(cx + r * Math.cos(a)).toFixed(2)} ${(cy + r * Math.sin(a)).toFixed(2)}`;

191	  const pts: string[] = [];

The glyph keys are: Grass, Fire, Water, Lightning, Psychic, Fighting, Darkness, Metal, Dragon, Colorless.

- `src/lib/glass.ts` — reuse `GLASS_DIALOG_PANEL`, `GLASS_DIALOG_GHOST_BUTTON`, `FOCUS_RING_INSET`, `GLASS_GHOST_BUTTON`.
- `src/components/ScrollArea.tsx` — for the scrollable details column (see its use in CoverDialog).
- `src/components/CardImage.tsx` — the image primitive (fill mode; graceful fallback). Use it for the big image.
- `src/components/icons.tsx` (or wherever `XIcon`, `CheckIcon` come from in CoverDialog) — find an appropriate "info"/"magnifier"/"search" icon for the inspect button; if none fits, add a small new icon following the existing icon style in that file, or reuse an existing one (e.g. a magnifier/info glyph). Prefer reusing.
- Find where `CardGrid` is rendered (grep for `<CardGrid` / `CardGridProps` — likely `src/features/builder/DeckBuilder.tsx`). That parent will own the modal state.

The `Card` shape (from `packages/schema/src/catalog/card.ts`): `{ id, setId, localId, name, category: "Pokemon"|"Trainer"|"Energy", image, illustrator, rarity, regulationMark, hp, stage, evolveFrom, types (string[]|null), retreat (int|null), abilities ({type?,name,effect?}[]|null), attacks ({cost?:string[],name,effect?,damage?:number|string}[]|null), weaknesses/resistances ({type,value?}[]|null), trainerType, energyType, effect (Trainer/Energy rules text|null), legal, variants }`.

```ts
export interface CardDetailDialogProps {
  open: boolean;
  /** The card to show — retained during the close so content doesn't blank out. Null before first open. */
  card: BuilderCard | null;
  onClose: () => void;
}
```
