- When `open` and `card` is set, fetch the full card with `getCard(card.cardId)` in an effect keyed on `card.cardId` (only fetch while open). Track `{ status: "loading"|"ready"|"error", data?: Card }`. **Guard against a stale response**: if the effect re-runs or unmounts, ignore the resolved promise (a cancelled flag). Show the known `card.name` in the header immediately (seed), so the header never flashes empty.
- **Loading**: header name (from the seed) + a subtle "Loading…" / skeleton in the body. **Error**: "Couldn't load card details" + a Retry button that re-runs the fetch.
- **Ready** — render:
  - Two-column on ≥sm (`sm:grid-cols-[...]`), stacked on mobile. Left: big image via `<CardImage fill imageUrl={card.hasImage ? cardImageUrl(id,"high") : undefined} .../>` in an `aspect-[2.5/3.5]` box. Right: a `ScrollArea` with the details.
  - Header block: name (big), a category chip, HP (Pokémon), and small chips for rarity + regulation mark when present.
  - Type pips: for each of `types`, render `<EnergyGlyph>` IF the string is a valid glyph key, else a small text chip. Write a tiny type-guard `isGlyphType(s: string): s is EnergyType` (a Set of the 10 keys) — put it in the dialog file or a small helper module; it must be unit-testable, so if it's a pure helper consider a named export.
  - Attacks (Pokémon): each attack as a row — a line of cost pips (map `attack.cost` strings through the same glyph/guard), the attack `name`, the `damage` right-aligned (render number or the modifier string as-is), and `effect` text beneath in muted color. Handle empty/no attacks gracefully (omit the section).
  - Abilities: each — a label from `ability.type` (fallback "Ability"), the `name`, and `effect`.
  - Weakness / Resistance / Retreat: a compact stat row. Weakness/resistance: type glyph (guarded) + `value`. Retreat: the integer (or that many Colorless pips — your call, keep it simple).
  - Trainer/Energy: when `category !== "Pokemon"` and `effect` is set, render the `effect` rules text as a paragraph block.
  - Footer meta: "Illus. {illustrator}" when present, and the set/number as plain text `{localId} · {setId}` (NO set-name lookup — the card payload doesn't carry it; keep it minimal and honest). evolveFrom ("Evolves from {evolveFrom}") when present.
- **Reduced motion**: any transition/scale you add must be gated with Tailwind's `motion-reduce:transition-none` (and avoid scale transforms under reduced motion). This new surface must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- TS strict, match the surrounding comment density and the explanatory-comment style of CoverDialog (a short "why" header comment at the top explaining the two-question interaction and the guard).

2. `CardTile`: add an **inspect button as a SIBLING of the tile `<button>`**, NOT a child (nesting `<button>` in `<button>` is invalid HTML). Place it as the last child of the `<li className="relative ...">`, absolutely positioned in a corner (e.g. `absolute right-1.5 top-1.5 z-20`), a small round glass button with the info/magnifier icon, `aria-label={`View ${card.name} details`}`. It should be visually subtle and **reveal on hover of the tile AND on its own keyboard focus** — e.g. `opacity-0 focus-visible:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 ...` with `group` added to the `<li>` (or the wrapper), plus `motion-reduce:transition-none`. On click → `onInspect(card)`. It must be keyboard-reachable (it's a real `<button>`, so it is). Ensure `type="button"`. Make sure it sits above the tile button so clicks land on it (z-index), and that clicking it does NOT add a copy (separate element, so it won't — but verify it isn't inside the tile button).
   - Keep the existing add/remove/drag behavior on the tile button 100% intact.
3. Parent (DeckBuilder or wherever CardGrid renders): add state `const [inspecting, setInspecting] = useState<BuilderCard | null>(null)` and `const [detailOpen, setDetailOpen] = useState(false)`. Pass `onInspect={(c) => { setInspecting(c); setDetailOpen(true); }}` to `<CardGrid>`. Render `<CardDetailDialog open={detailOpen} card={inspecting} onClose={() => setDetailOpen(false)} />` alongside the existing dialogs (e.g. next to where CoverDialog / ImportExportDialog are rendered). Keep `inspecting` set through the close so content doesn't blank (mirror how CoverDialog is wired if it uses the same idiom).

## Tests (Vitest)
- Add `src/features/builder/components/CardDetailDialog.test.tsx` with `// @vitest-environment jsdom` at the top. FIRST check whether an existing dialog test (e.g. a CoverDialog/ImportExportDialog `.test.tsx`, grep `showModal` in tests) already establishes how these native-`<dialog>` components are tested under jsdom — MIRROR that setup (jsdom may need `HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal`/`close` spied/mocked). If no dialog test exists, mock `showModal`/`close` on the prototype in a `beforeEach`.
  - Mock `getCard` (from `../../../lib/api`) with `vi.mock`. Test: (a) opening with a card triggers `getCard(cardId)` and renders the name + an attack name + an ability + illustrator once resolved; (b) the loading state shows the seeded name; (c) the error state renders on a rejected `getCard` and Retry re-invokes it; (d) the close button calls `onClose`.
- If you extracted `isGlyphType` as a pure export, add a tiny unit test for it (valid key → true, unknown string like "Colorless"/"Water" true, "Bogus" false) — or fold that assertion into the component test if inline.
- Do NOT weaken or delete existing tests. Match existing test style (look at a neighboring `*.test.tsx`).

## Definitely do NOT
- Do NOT change the API/DB/schema/ingest, or promise pricing / national-dex-number / flavor-text (they are NOT stored — don't reference them).
- Do NOT change the tile's click=add / right-click=remove / drag semantics.
- Do NOT add new npm deps.

All green: typecheck clean, biome clean, 5/5 new tests pass, and the full builder suite (15 files / 134 tests) still passes.

## Summary

### Files created
- `src/features/builder/components/CardDetailDialog.tsx` — the modal. Native `<dialog>` mirroring CoverDialog (showModal/close on `open`, `onClose`, backdrop click-to-dismiss, `aria-labelledby` a `useId` title, header close button). Fetches via `getCard(card.cardId)` in an effect keyed on `[open, cardId, retryNonce]`, gated to fetch only while open, with a `cancelled` flag guarding stale responses. Header name is seeded from the `BuilderCard` so it never flashes empty. States: loading (skeleton + "Loading…"), error ("Couldn't load card details" + Retry that bumps `retryNonce`), ready (two-column ≥sm / stacked mobile: big `CardImage` left in an `aspect-[2.5/3.5]` box, `ScrollArea` details right). Details render type pips, abilities, attacks (cost pips + name + right-aligned damage + effect), a weakness/resistance/retreat "Combat" row, Trainer/Energy `effect` text, and footer meta (evolveFrom / Illus. / `{localId} · {setId}` plain text). Exports a pure `isGlyphType(s): s is EnergyType` guard backed by a Set of the 10 keys.
- `src/features/builder/components/CardDetailDialog.test.tsx` — jsdom, mocks `../../../lib/api` (`getCard` + `cardImageUrl`), `installDomShims` for `showModal`/`close`. Covers: fetch-on-open renders name/attack/ability/illustrator/set-number; loading shows seeded name; error + Retry re-invokes `getCard`; close button calls `onClose`; plus an `isGlyphType` unit test.

### Files modified
- `src/features/builder/components/CardGrid.tsx` — added required `onInspect: (card: BuilderCard) => void` to `CardGridProps`, threaded through `TileHandlers` (`Pick` + destructure). Added `group` to the tile `<li>` and an inspect `<button>` as the **last sibling** of the `<li>` (not nested in the tile button): `absolute right-1.5 top-1.5 z-20`, round glass, `InfoIcon`, `aria-label={`View ${card.name} details`}`, `type="button"`, `opacity-0 focus-visible:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity motion-reduce:transition-none`. Add/remove/drag on the tile button are untouched.
- `src/features/builder/DeckBuilder.tsx` — added `inspecting`/`detailOpen` state, `onInspect` prop to `<CardGrid>`, and `<CardDetailDialog>` rendered beside CoverDialog. `inspecting` is kept set through close.
- `src/components/icons.tsx` — added `InfoIcon` (circled "i").

### Exact interaction
Hovering a grid tile (or keyboard-focusing its corner button) reveals a circled-i button; clicking it opens the detail modal for that card without adding a copy (separate sibling element). The modal shows the card name immediately, fetches full details, and renders them; Escape/backdrop/close button dismiss it; the card stays populated through the close animation.

### Deviations from spec (with why)
- **New `InfoIcon` instead of reusing an icon.** Spec preferred reuse but permitted adding one; the existing magnifier (`SearchIcon`) reads as "search" (already the grid's search field), so a circled-i is the unambiguous "view details" affordance.
- **`Card` imported from `@luminous/schema`, not `../../../lib/api`.** `api.ts` does not re-export `Card` (spec's example implied `type Card` from api). Functional import (`getCard`, `cardImageUrl`) is still from `lib/api`.
- **Type/cost pips are colored** via the existing `ENERGY_TYPE_META` palette (passed as `fill`); spec said "render `<EnergyGlyph>`" — this is a low-risk polish using existing data.
- **Retreat rendered as Colorless pips** ("Free" when 0) — spec explicitly left this to my call.
- **Test filename is `CardDetailDialog.test.tsx`** (per the spec's explicit name + its verification command), whereas the repo's DOM-test convention is `*.dom.test.tsx`. The `// @vitest-environment jsdom` docblock makes it run correctly under the vitest include glob either way.

### What to verify in the browser
1. Hover a grid card: the corner info button fades in; Tab to it with the keyboard: it appears on focus.
2. Click it: modal opens with the card name instantly, then attacks/abilities/weakness/retreat/illustrator/set-number fill in.
3. Confirm clicking the info button does NOT add a copy, and the tile's click=add / right-click=remove / drag still work.
4. Inspect a Trainer and an Energy card: no types/attacks sections, and the rules `effect` text shows.
5. A card with `hasImage=false`: left panel shows the neutral fallback, not a broken image.
6. Kill the API (or a bad id) to see the error state, then Retry.
7. Backdrop click, Escape, and the X all close it; reopening a different card refetches.
8. With `prefers-reduced-motion` on, the inspect-button reveal has no transition and nothing scales.

Note: I did not touch API/DB/schema/ingest, added no npm deps, and did not run SFTP upload (out of scope for this dev/verify slice).

# Verifying luminous_ui end-to-end

Two servers, then drive the web GUI with agent-browser.

## Launch

```bash
# API (Cloudflare Worker, local D1/KV/R2 state under apps/api/.wrangler):
cd apps/api && SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt bun run dev   # :8787
# SSL_CERT_FILE is a NixOS quirk: workerd needs it for origin fetches
# (the lazy tcgdex→R2 asset mirror). Node-side CLIs and production are fine.

# Web (Vite):
bun run dev    # 127.0.0.1:5173
```

## Gotchas that will eat your session

- **Browse via `http://localhost:5173`, NEVER `http://127.0.0.1:5173`.** The
  api's CORS allows exactly `APP_ORIGIN` (= `http://localhost:5173` in dev);
  from 127.0.0.1 every fetch fails and the UI shows "Couldn't reach the
  server". Vite serves both, so the page *renders* either way.
- **agent-browser:** the `~/.cargo/bin/agent-browser` on PATH is broken
  ("required file not found"); use `/etc/profiles/per-user/jofre/bin/agent-browser`.
  `screenshot` sometimes times out (CDP `Page.captureScreenshot`) — rely on
  `snapshot -i` / `get text body` for evidence instead.
- **agent-browser clicks can silently no-op after a page reload** (report
  "✓ Done", nothing happens — observed 2026-07-16 on /play): `click @ref` and
  `find role button click` both affected, and `drag` can hang the daemon for
  its full 120 s timeout. When clicks stop landing, switch to
  `eval '(()=>{const b=[...document.querySelectorAll("button")].find(x=>x.textContent==="…"); return b?(b.click(),"ok"):"missing";})()'`
  — wrap in an IIFE (bare `const` collides across evals). Evidence-gather via
  `eval`+`querySelectorAll` too; the a11y snapshot can lag the real DOM.
- **Drags DO work on the Pixi playmat** (pointer-event synthesis via CDP):
  `drag '[data-card-owner="you"][data-card-zone="hand"][data-card-index="N"]' '[data-card-owner="you"][data-card-zone="active"]'`
  — the drop-zone anchors carry `data-card-owner`/`data-card-zone`(/`data-card-index`
  for hand slots). Hand indexes re-pack after each placement.
- **Session cookies are HttpOnly** — you can't extract them for curl. To hit
  authed api routes with the browser's session, use
  `agent-browser eval 'fetch("http://localhost:8787/…",{credentials:"include"}).then(r=>r.text())'`.
- The api access log is the ground truth for writes: grep the wrangler dev
  output for `PATCH /decks` etc. Builder saves debounce ~600 ms and coalesce —
  expect ONE PATCH per burst of edits.
- The app is wrapped in React **StrictMode**: dev double-mounts everything.
  Anything effect/cleanup-shaped (savers, sockets) must survive it — verify
  such flows in the dev server, not just the prod build.
- **Promote and Retreat on /play are HUD dialogs, not drags** — dragging
  bench→active during ko:promote reports "✓ Done" but silently no-ops. Click
  the Pokémon button inside `[aria-label="Promote a Pokémon"]`; retreat:
  select N energies + the switch-in, then the dialog's Retreat button.
- **The real-game bench drop zone has no `data-card-index`** — target
  `[data-card-owner="you"][data-card-zone="bench"]` bare; only the
  simulator's empty slots carry indexes.
- **Damage/status chips are `pointer-events:none`**, so `elementFromPoint`
  skips them — to prove paint order, temporarily set
  `style.pointerEvents="auto"` on the chip AND its wrapper, hit-test,
  restore.
- Pass turn is an icon button (`button[aria-label="Pass turn"]`); prize picks
  are `button[aria-label^="Prize"]` + a "Take N/N" confirm.

## Data / accounts

- Local D1 is small by design and drifts from remote (19 sets / 3,698 cards).
  As of 2026-07-16 it holds sve, sv06.5, sv01, sv02, sv03 (~890 cards) — the
  last three ingested for the /play demo decks. **Check, don't trust this
  list** (`wrangler d1 execute luminous --local --command "SELECT set_id,
  COUNT(*) FROM cards GROUP BY set_id"`): `.wrangler` state has been wiped

  (comma-separated, ~30 s/set).
- Register throwaway accounts freely (`*@example.com`, password ≥8 chars);
  local KV rate-limits login/register bursts (429) — space attempts out.
- OAuth routes answer 503 locally until secrets exist — the UI copy
  "… sign-in isn't set up yet" is the *correct* outcome.

## Flows worth driving

- Anonymous gates: `/decks` and `/decks/:id/edit` show sign-in prompts; the
  Sign in link carries `state.from` and returns you to the exact URL.
- Register → lands on `/decks`. Create deck (server-minted UUID) → rename
  inline → open → add cards in the builder → "Saved" appears → reload → cards
  still there (and `GET /decks` shows the real cardCount).
- Card art must come from `localhost:8787/assets/cards/<id>/low.webp` with
  nonzero `naturalWidth` (lazy tcgdex mirror, needs SSL_CERT_FILE above).
- Folder delete lifts contents up one level: watch the log for
  PATCH(es) *before* the DELETE.
- **/play (local hot-seat game):** demo decks work anonymously; Start game
  fan-outs `GET /cards/:id` for the pool (needs the sets above in local D1 —
  missing ids surface as a friendly error naming them). Setup placements and
  energy attaches are drags (see the drag recipe above); attacks/retreat/
  prize-picks are HUD buttons. Input gates on the projection's `waitingOn`;
  the screen flips to whoever must act (incl. the KO'd defender's promote).

127:| D86 | A deck cover is a PIN over the derived default, resolved on read (P5 polish, increment P5-6) | P5-3 fronted every deck with its highest-HP Pokémon and said outright that the proper answer was letting the owner choose. This is that: a nullable `decks.cover_card_id` the editor sets, and a pure **`effectiveCoverCardId(chosen, candidates)`** the list query runs — **the pin wins, and everything else falls through to `pickCoverCardId`**. The derived rule is untouched; it is now explicitly the DEFAULT rather than the answer. **Three decisions carry the slice.** First, **the resolution runs against the candidate list the default was already deriving from**, so honouring a choice costs NO extra query, and a pin that has gone stale (its card removed elsewhere, or its scan gone after a re-ingest) silently falls back instead of drawing a blank rectangle — a deck must never front a card it doesn't run. Second, **the pin may be a TRAINER or an Energy while the derived default stays Pokémon-only**: guessing needs a rule, choosing does not, and a signature Supporter is a legitimate face (browser-verified with Academy at Night, which the rule could never pick). Third, **two fields, deliberately not one**: `DeckSummary.coverCardId` remains the face being DRAWN (so the grid needed no change at all), while the full `Deck` carries `chosenCoverCardId`, the stored CHOICE the editor's picker is set to — null for almost every deck. Collapsing them into one name would have made "what is drawn" and "what was chosen" the same word for two different questions. **`Automatic` is an explicit option in the picker**, not the absence of one, so reverting is one click; it deliberately shows no art, because the default is a RULE and drawing today's answer to it would read as "this card". **The consistency rule lives on both sides:** PATCH validates the pin against the card list the patch LEAVES BEHIND (400 `cover card not in deck`) and drops a pin whose card that patch removes, while the editor's `toSnapshot` drops it locally too — not cosmetic, since the cover rides the same debounced PATCH as the card list, and a self-contradicting body would 400 forever (the saver retries the same dirty snapshot). The cover joining that one save path is what keeps the pair atomic. 1911 → **1932** tests; migration `0004`. **BROWSER-VERIFIED end to end at 1920×1080:** pinning the Trainer put it on the library tile, removing it dropped the pin, kept saving ("Saved", PATCH 200 — the wedge that would have followed a naive implementation) and fell back to Absol; a pin survived a reload through GET /decks/:id; a hand-crafted PATCH naming a card outside the deck got the 400; and both the footer control and a picker tile hit-tested to themselves. *Why: a heuristic that is right most of the time plus an override that is always right beats trying to make the heuristic cleverer — and the override is only trustworthy if the two can never disagree about what the deck contains.* (2026-07-26) |
128:| D87 | A favourite deck is a validated PIN of the account's OWN deck, resolved on read (P5 polish, increment P5-7) | Joins P5-5 (an editable profile) and P5-6 (a deck's cover art): an account pins one of its own decks as its favourite and sees that deck's cover + name on /settings. A nullable **`users.favourite_deck_id`** (migration `0005`) surfaced as **`userSchema.favouriteDeckId`** — **just the ID.** **Three choices.** First, **store only the id, not the deck's name/cover:** /settings resolves those from the caller's own `GET /decks` list, so a rename or re-cover shows through with no stale copy and a favourite whose deck has vanished resolves to a blank tile — the SAME "derive on read, tolerate stale" the covers use (D83/D86). Second, **a favourite must be one of YOUR decks:** `PATCH /auth/me` gains an OPTIONAL nullable `favouriteDeckId` (absent leaves it, null clears it, a string is validated against the caller's decks) and 400s `favourite deck not found` for anyone else's id or a phantom — the account can never point at a deck it doesn't own, mirroring D86's `cover card not in deck`. Third, **the FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL`** so deleting a favourited deck clears the pin rather than blocking the delete (a RESTRICT FK would) or dangling a stale id; D1 enforces FKs here (the deck DELETE leans on `deck_cards`' cascade), and since drizzle-kit drops the referential action on an ADD COLUMN, migration 0005 restores `ON DELETE SET NULL` by hand. The users↔decks mutual reference forced an `AnySQLiteColumn` annotation to break the TS type cycle. The picker is a native `<select>` in the SAME form as the name, riding ONE PATCH so name + favourite save atomically; the provider adopts the answer, so the corner control follows with no re-probe. 1932 → **1936** tests. Browser-verified end to end 2026-07-27 (build #71): pin on /settings → cover (`sv06.5-012`, real art) + name render + `PATCH /auth/me` 200; survives reload; `DELETE`ing the deck clears `favouriteDeckId` to null server-side (the FK) and the tile goes blank. Also covered by a DOM round-trip test + schema units. *Why: the profile only needs to REFERENCE a deck, and the deck already owns its name and cover — copying them onto the account would just be a second source of truth to keep in sync; the id plus resolve-on-read is the whole feature, and the validated pin + SET NULL make "your favourite is always a real deck of yours" true by construction.* (2026-07-27) |

## Product / architecture decisions
| # | Decision | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Backend data strategy | Own DB — ingest tcgdex → Cloudflare D1, serve our own API |
| D2 | Accounts & persistence | Full accounts + auth; users own their decks |
| D2a | Auth methods | Email + password **and** social OAuth (Discord + Google) |
| D3 | Catalog scope | Full-history-capable schema, ingest SV-era first |
| D4 | Card images | Mirror into R2, serve from our domain |
| D5 | Card type | Unify — one canonical `Card`; builder/playmat are view projections |
| D6 | Online lobby server | In scope — real Durable Object (WebSocket) lobby |
| D7 | Game engine placement | Separate **`packages/engine`** (pure logic) — imported by both `apps/web` (local play) and `apps/api` (authoritative DO). *Why: the engine runs in two runtimes; an app can't import another app.* |
| D8 | Card-effect modeling | **Composable, data-driven op programs** over shared archetype templates (not per-card functions); engine emits **semantic events** consumed by the animation layer. *Why: cards are minor variations on a few archetypes; keeps authoring + animation cheap. Detail in `workstreams/simulator.md`.* |
| D9 | Image mirroring & ingest execution (refines D4/§3.4) | Images mirror into R2 **lazily** — a Worker route (`GET /assets/…`) serves from R2 and on miss fetches tcgdex origin, stores, streams; catalog rows keep tcgdex **origin** URLs. Card-data backfill runs as a **local Bun script** applying batched upsert SQL via `wrangler d1 execute`; a future cron does small in-Worker deltas only. *Why: a full SV backfill is ~10k images — over Worker subrequest limits in one shot and hours of CLI puts; cache-aside mirrors exactly what's viewed and stays within limits.* (2026-07-09) |
| D10 | M9 catalog search shape (refines D5/§6) | `CardBrief` **extended** with `types/hp/regulationMark/stage/trainerType/energyType` (card-table columns only — **no set join**, so no `setName`); `GET /cards` gains **repeatable `type`/`rarity`** (OR within a dimension) and **`sort=name\|hp-desc\|set`**; KV cache keys version-prefixed (`catalog:v2:`) so a shape change can't serve stale briefs. The builder consumes briefs through one adapter (`src/features/builder/catalog.ts` — accented `"Pokémon"`, stage/trainerType/energyType → the single `subtype`). *Why: the grid/filters/deck-math need those fields per tile; per-tile full-Card fetches or a fixture pool were the alternatives.* (2026-07-13) |
| D11 | M9 scope trims (pending P2) | **Kinds** (`subtypes`) filter stays a client-side per-page heuristic (server can't express OR across stage/trainerType; EX/Mega are name-regexes until structured data — P2 tasks 8-9). **Manual deck/folder reorder is session-only** (no position field in the schema — P2 task 17). **Folder delete keeps the lift-up UX client-side** (child PATCHes before DELETE) over the server's cascade semantics. **`RARITIES` is a hardcoded tcgdex vocabulary snapshot** in the rail. *Why: each would widen M9's already-large surface; all four are logged with their fixes in `workstreams/deck-builder.md`.* (2026-07-13) **Revised 2026-07-14 (P2-M1):** kinds now filter **server-side** (repeatable `stage`/`trainerType`/`energyType`) — only EX/Mega remain a client-side name-regex post-filter (tcgdex `suffix` not persisted; follow-up logged); hardcoded vocabularies replaced by **`GET /facets`**. Reorder (task 17) and lift-up remain as decided. **Revised again 2026-07-14 (task 17):** reorder is now persisted — see D13; only the lift-up trim still stands. |
| D12 | P2-M1 catalog surface & legality source of truth | `GET /cards` gains **repeatable `id`** (≤100, deck hydration in ONE call; chunked IN + in-memory ordering twin of the SQL sort), **`nameExact`** (case-insensitive whole-name equality), `serie`, `illustrator`, `text` (LIKE over ability/attack JSON), plus the kind params above; **`GET /facets`** serves the filter vocabularies (7 DISTINCTs, one db.batch, KV-cached). `CardBrief` += **`legal {standard,expanded}`**; KV namespace → **`catalog:v3:`**, with KV **bypassed** for >512-byte keys and any `?id=` request (per-deck id sets never recur — caching them is pure write waste). Web: **`Format.legalFlag`** keys BOTH the `legalOnly` filter (`legal=<flag>`) and `isLegalInFormat` (structured verdict beats printed mark; mark check only for legal-less fixtures) — one legality definition for grid + validator. Deck rules: **Radiant = 1 per deck total** (like ACE SPEC; official rule), Prism Star = 1 per name. *Why: filters needed server truth for correct totals; hydration was an N-request fan-out; legality had two disagreeing definitions.* (2026-07-14) |
| D13 | Manual-order persistence model (P2 task 17) | `position` INTEGER on `decks` and `folders` — **global per user, not per folder**: the web grid's flat array (position-ascending) IS the manual order, per-view filtering preserves relative order, and a nest move keeps the row's slot (folderId changes, position doesn't) — exactly the client's existing semantics. Creates take **min−1** (new rows prepend); migration 0003 backfills existing rows in the old name-order so nothing visibly moves. Public cards key off the engine **uid** so the Pixi layer animates a card as one object across projections. The phase mapping is an **exhaustive switch** (`satisfies never`) — a new engine phase is a compile error, not a silent guess. *Why: this is the same per-viewer filter P4's server will apply; building it client-side first pins the contract with tests.* (2026-07-16) **Revised 2026-07-17 (wire-up review):** during any `setup:*` phase the OPPONENT's active/bench also project as face-down backs (positional `-hidden` ids, no `pokemon` rows — a row would leak the uid key + printed HP); a hot-seat viewer flip at Ready was exposing the first player's face-down placements. | D78 | The spectator view is `redactGame(..., spectating)` — one gate, both sides symmetric (P4 online, increment 3c-vii-a) | Spectate is the last item on the P4 plan, and it splits cleanly: this is the HIDDEN-INFORMATION half, landed on its own so it can be reviewed as a security change rather than buried in transport and UI (the 2b-iii-a precedent — the seam before its consumer). **The threat model is the decision.** A spectator is not a stranger: the realistic attacker is a PLAYER who opens a spectator view of the match they are playing to read the other hand. [] : …` branches that the next affordance added there could silently miss. That is not tidiness: `trainers`/`abilities`/`rareCandy` name cards **in the actor's hand**, so leaking them would undo the hand redaction two lines above. | D79 | The lobby link IS the spectate link — a refused seat becomes a spectator (P4 online, increment 3c-vii-b) | Wiring 3c-vii-a's seatless redaction to real viewers, with the design constraint that it add **no new frame, no new URL and no invite flow**. Their safety is structural twice over — every handler that can change the game gates on `attachedPlayer`, which stays null for them, and the board they receive is the one that withholds both hands. `attachPlayer` clears the flag, so a watcher who later takes a freed seat stops getting the seatless board. **Players are NOT told they are being watched** — chosen deliberately: telling them needs a spectator count on the wire and a broadcast on every join/leave, and the lobby already treats a refused socket silently. What they get is a public table — both boards, no hands, no deck order, no prizes — which is the intended product behaviour, not an oversight. **Client:** `useLobby`'s sticky `rejected` boolean became `refusal: "full" | "kicked" | null`, because the two are no longer the same thing — a KICK is terminal, while "full" keeps the connection, keeps accepting `state` (for the players' names) and `match` (the board), and flips the status to `spectating` on the first board. | D80 | Half-open sockets are swept with the runtime's OWN keepalive timestamp (P4 online, increment 3c-viii) | The gap 3c-v's browser run surfaced, and the last known way an online match could stall. `setWebSocketAutoResponse` answers the client's 1.5s ping without waking the DO — the thing that makes hibernation worth having — but it also means the DO can never notice pings that STOP. A network that dies without a TCP close therefore left a socket that looked perfectly live forever: `hasSocket` said yes, no disconnect grace was armed, no forfeit clock started, and the opponent waited indefinitely. Every ORDINARY exit (tab close, browser kill, navigation, reload, crash) delivers a close event, which is why this never bit in practice and why it took a deliberate `set offline` to reproduce. **The fix is to read the signal the runtime was already recording:** `state.getWebSocketAutoResponseTimestamp(ws)` returns when it last auto-answered that socket, so liveness costs nothing at ping time. The alternative — dropping the auto-response and stamping `lastSeen` in `webSocketMessage` — was rejected on exactly that ground: it would wake the DO ~40 times a minute per socket and give up hibernation to learn what the runtime already knows. **What it costs instead is a POLL**, because a quiet in-game lobby schedules no alarm at all: `scheduleMaintenance` now pushes a `LIVENESS_SWEEP_MS` (30s) deadline whenever any socket is connected, so an occupied lobby wakes twice a minute. `SOCKET_SILENCE_MS` is 15s — ten missed pings, so a phone changing networks or a throttled background tab is not mistaken for a dead one — and a test pins the budget that matters: sweep + silence + the 5s grace all fit inside the 90s forfeit, so a dead network can never resolve slower than a closed tab. **A `null` timestamp counts as ALIVE**, deliberately: it is the state of every connection before its first ping, and nothing can distinguish "just opened" from "opened long ago and never pinged" — the cost of that reading is a socket we never sweep, versus closing a healthy one-second-old connection. **The sweep only CLOSES**; everything after it — the grace, the seat going disconnected, the forfeit — is the machinery a real close already drives, reached through the same `socketGone` (called explicitly, since a server-side `close()` delivers no `webSocketClose` event to us). 1874 → **1878** tests. **BROWSER-VERIFIED with the very reproducer that exposed the bug:** with a match live, one client was put offline with the socket left open; before this change that produced nothing at all, and now the opponent saw "disconnected — forfeits in 1:30" after ~50s (15s silence + up to 30s sweep + the 5s grace) and the countdown ran. Bringing the client back online restored it within ~10s — the channel reconnected, re-helloed, and the forfeit was cancelled — while the client that stayed connected throughout was never swept. Zero page errors. *Why: the cheapest signal is the one someone else is already recording. Hibernation exists to avoid waking on keepalives, so any fix that inspects keepalives directly is self-defeating; asking the runtime when it last answered turns a per-ping cost into a per-half-minute one.* (2026-07-26) |

| D83 | A deck's cover is its highest-HP Pokémon, derived on read (P5 polish, increment P5-3) | The decks grid drew the same blue card back for every deck under a generated tint, while the catalog has had real scans since P2. **The slice's whole content is the RULE**, so it lives in a pure `pickCoverCardId` that can be argued with and tested rather than inside SQL: **the Pokémon with the highest printed HP**, ties broken by copies, then by card id for determinism. Cards with no scan are skipped rather than picked and rendered blank, and a deck with no qualifying card gets `coverCardId: null`, keeping the card back — which is also exactly right for a deck you have only just created (`fromDeck`, the create-response mapper, hardcodes null for that reason). **Derived on READ**, in one extra query for the whole library beside the existing `cardCount` aggregate: no stored column, so a cover follows the deck's contents with nothing to keep in sync, and no write path to change. ## Locked assumptions (override explicitly if they change)
- Bun-workspace monorepo; API + Lobby DO on Cloudflare **Workers** via `wrangler`.
- **Hono** + **Zod**; **Drizzle** over D1. Ingest uses **plain REST fetch +
  our Zod schemas** — the official `@tcgdex/sdk` turned out unnecessary since
  we validate every payload ourselves anyway (changed 2026-07-09, was: SDK).
- Server **sessions** (http-only cookie), not stateless JWT.
- Ingest filters to SV-era but writes the full-history schema.
- attacks/weaknesses/resistances stored as JSON columns for now (promote to
  child tables only if we need to query inside them).
- English (`en`) first; schema leaves room for i18n later.
- The **match engine (P3)** is the actual gameplay; approximate at first,
  improved iteratively.

## These are defaults, not law
Every decision and assumption here is a **default with a rationale**, chosen with
the context available at the time — revisit any of them when the code or new
context reveals a better path. The point of writing them down is to preserve the
*why*, so a later session can judge whether it still holds.

Append a row (or a dated subsection for bigger ones) with the choice **and the
one-line why**. When you revise an existing decision, update its row and note
what changed and why. The one hard rule: **don't reverse a decision silently** —
leave a trail so the reasoning is never lost.

They were mock chrome from the /simulator prototype, so "history navigation is unreachable during your own turn:action" described navigation that did not exist. Two buttons a screen reader announced as "Previous"/"Forward" and that did nothing are worse than none; they are gone. If a real history is built, they come back WIRED. - **The playmat's ⟶ was enabled exactly when the panel covered it** — the panel renders precisely when `passDisabled === false` — so on /play and online it was never clickable. `PlaymatView.onPassTurn` is now OPTIONAL and the control renders only for a driver that passes one: the /simulator sandbox, where nothing covers it. Nothing stored, nothing uploaded, and the same person looks the same to you in every lobby; an anonymous seat keeps the generic figure rather than being given a face that would change next visit. Saturation and lightness are FIXED so the seed picks the hue and never how loud the result is. **Still open: uploaded avatars** — the item below (R2 + CSP); an image simply wins over the generated one when it lands. - **Profiles — NAME + FACE DONE 2026-07-26 (P5-5, D85); favourite deck open.** The Profile section on **/settings** (`src/features/settings/ ProfileSection.tsx`) is where an account edits itself, and the first thing it fixes is that P5-1 made your name authoritative and broadcast while leaving it unchangeable. **`PATCH /auth/me`** (requireUser BEFORE the validator; no write when nothing changed) takes `updateProfileRequestSchema` — one required `displayName`, trimmed, 1–64, the same bounds register applies to its optional one. Deriving the hash client-side was rejected — a second copy of FNV-1a is one that must agree with the server forever.
